commits.pr_title: [XPU] Add tuned Mamba SSU configs for Intel Arc Pro B60
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`selective_state_update` picks its Triton launch config from a per-device JSON
keyed on `(headdim, dstate, device_name, cache_dtype)`. #50534 added that
lookup and shipped configs for Intel Arc Pro B70. Intel Arc Pro B60 has no
entry, so every B60 run falls back to the heuristic.

This PR adds the missing B60 files. No code changes.

## Changes

Eight config files under
`vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/ops/configs/selective_state_update/`, one
per `(shape, cache_dtype)` pair, across four `(headdim, dstate)` shapes:

- `headdim=64, dstate=128` — float16 and float32 (Mamba2 family, Zamba2-1.2B,
  Nemotron-H-8B, Granite-4.0-h-tiny, Falcon-H1-0.5B)
- `headdim=128, dstate=256` — float16 and float32 (Falcon-H1-3B/7B/34B)
- `headdim=64, dstate=64` — float16 and float32 (Zamba2-2.7B)
- `headdim=64, dstate=256` — float16 and float32 (Falcon-H1-1.5B(-Deep))

The first two shapes are the same ones the B70 PR shipped, so the two devices
are directly comparable; the latter two cover Zamba2 and Falcon-H1 checkpoints
the B70 PR did not exercise.

## Method

Generated on a single Intel Arc Pro B60 (23.91 GiB) with the in-tree
`benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_selective_state_update.py --save-configs`,
sweeping effective batch 8..131072, on vLLM 0.28.0 / torch 2.13.0+xpu.

### Triton version

All eight files record `"triton_version": "3.8.0"`. They were first tuned on
Triton 3.7.x, then re-checked on Triton 3.8.0 (torch 2.14.0+xpu, one B60 per
shape, tune and cross-eval in the same pod). Seven shapes keep their winners:
the shipped config is within 1.006-1.036x geomean of the best re-measured one.
`headdim=64, dstate=128, float16` moved on 3.8.0 (shipped config 1.10x geomean,
up to 1.99x slower at small batch), so that file now holds the 3.8.0 winners for
effective batch 8..32768 and keeps the 65536/131072 entries from the original
sweep. The end-to-end numbers below were measured with the Triton 3.7.x configs
and not repeated on 3.8.0.

## Results

### Numerical validation

Every shipped config (all 8 shape/cache_dtype combinations) was validated
against the fp32 reference (`--validate`) across the capped batch grid
8..2048 (9 points) — all 72 checks passed.

### Kernel speedup

Heuristic vs. tuned, `--compare`, on the first two (B70-comparable) shapes:

| shape | cache_dtype | geomean | min | max |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| headdim=64, dstate=128 | float16 | 3.36x | 1.42x | 4.91x |
| headdim=64, dstate=128 | float32 | 2.68x | 1.26x | 6.38x |
| headdim=128, dstate=256 | float16 | 6.12x | 3.73x | 10.26x |
| headdim=128, dstate=256 | float32 | 3.83x | 3.05x | 7.27x |

Overall geomean **3.71x** across 54 (shape, cache_dtype, batch) entries; every
single entry improves over the heuristic.

### End-to-end

`vllm serve` + `vllm bench serve`, 512 in / 128 out, 32 prompts, paired by rep,
arms alternating base/tuned within each rep. Base is the pristine package (no
B60 file present); tuned installs the configs above.

| model | shape | base tok/s | tuned tok/s | speedup | reps won |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Zyphra/Zamba2-1.2B-instruct (run 1) | 64,128 | 490.05 | 568.08 | +15.92% | 6/6 |
| Zyphra/Zamba2-1.2B-instruct (run 2) | 64,128 | 500.00 | 658.53 | +31.71% | 6/6 |
| Zyphra/Zamba2-2.7B-instruct | 64,64 | 133.47 | 136.16 | +2.02% | 6/6 |
| tiiuae/Falcon-H1-3B-Instruct | 128,256 | 296.51 | 651.06 | +119.57% | 6/6 |
| tiiuae/Falcon-H1-1.5B-Instruct | 64,256 | 504.41 | 780.34 | +54.70% | 6/6 |

All five runs are significant under a paired permutation test (p=0.0321, the
smallest a 6-pair test can report), and tuned wins every rep in every run.

## Test plan

- Regenerate with `benchmark_selective_state_update.py --save-configs` on B60
  and confirm the same winners.
- `--validate` every shipped key; a failing config is dropped, not shipped.
- Serve a Mamba2/Zamba2/Falcon-H1 model on B60 and confirm the tuned file is
  the one loaded.
- No CUDA/ROCm behaviour changes: this PR is data only.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Trim the last KV-source layer in decoder replay
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

In decoder replay steps, the last KV-source layer (layer 20 on DSV4.1-Flash) still ran on every row, though for the trimmed rows only its KV (SWA, compressed, index K) is read. Its indexer scoring and top-k, sparse MLA, wo and MoE feed only the replay layers.

- The cut layer now writes its KV for every row (`DeepseekV4DecoderLayer.write_kv` → `DeepseekV4Attention.forward_kv`), then runs as the first replay layer (`decoder_replay_start = cut`) on the replay rows, in the replay batch and its CUDA graphs. Its sliding-window metadata keeps the batch's window starts, so it stays exact. The indexer row-buffer compaction goes.
- PIECEWISE graphs now decide the replay break (and `write_kv`) by graph size (`DecoderReplayLayers.replays()`) instead of `replay_batch is not None`, which is unset at capture: before, the break was never captured and PIECEWISE steps did not trim.

## Results

DSV4.1-Flash DEP4 on B200, CUDA graphs up to 8192 tokens, `vllm bench serve` random. Baseline: #59532 with PIECEWISE trimming working, layer 20 not cut.

| | baseline | this PR | |

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] structured decisions: noul and score question types
commits.pr_body:
Lands on top of #59299, adding two more question types.

Note: this is landing in parallel with diffusiongemma support (#60466) and a rough merge branch is available here: https://github.com/mmastrac/vllm/tree/systemone-question-types-dgemma

## Overview

Adds the two question types the /v1/systemone contract defines beyond choice, following the Jev API shapes:

- `noul`: yes or no. `criteria` is null, or an object with optional `true` and `false` descriptions. Any other key is a 400. The labels are `yes` and `no`. The answer carries the probability of yes.
- `score`: rate the state on an ordered list of 2 to 10 levels. The labels are `0` to `9`, the same index the answer uses. The answer is the expected level, a legend of level names, and probabilities by level index.

Each question type declares its labels with `label_set`. The read strategy finds the token for every registered type's labels at startup, and fails there if one is not a single distinct token after the chat prompt.

## Claims

JevBench public items (231: 139 choice, 74 noul, 18 score), one read per item, thinking off. "Mapped" sends noul and score items as `choice` questions over the task's labels, which is all main supports. "Native" sends them as `noul` and `score`. Choice items read the same in both runs.

Smaller Qwen3 models are included solely for comparison purposes - these models would not be recommended for general use. Their solve rates do appear worse, but the models are noisy and no sampling was performed. 

| model | run | Intelligence | noul | score | label_mass (noul / score) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-0.6B | mapped | 26.1 | 43/74 | 7/18 | 0.98 / 0.89 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | native | 21.4 | 36/74 | 6/18 | 0.98 / 1.00 |
| Qwen3-4B | mapped | 52.7 | 48/74 | 11/18 | 0.93 / 0.84 |
| Qwen3-4B | native | 47.3 | 43/74 | 8/18 | 0.99 / 0.99 |
| DiffusionGemma 26B | mapped | 79.0 | 58/74 | 16/18 | 0.97 / 0.91 |
| DiffusionGemma 26B | native | 80.6 | 62/74 | 13/18 | 0.96 / 0.92 |

- **Noul**: option order explains the Qwen gap. JevBench lists "no" first, and the noul prompt lists "yes" first. On Qwen3-4B the same items as a `choice` score 48/74 with "no" first and 42/74 with "yes" first, against 43/74 native. On DiffusionGemma, native noul beats both orders (60/74 and 58/74).
- **Score**: native trails by 1 to 3 of 18 items on every model. The digit-labeled reads favor level 2 (11 of 18 items on Qwen3-4B, 6 expected). 18 items are too few to settle it, so the labels stay `0` to `9` to match the answer and #60676.
- DiffusionGemma reads are not exactly repeatable: choice items scored 121 and 122 on two runs of unchanged requests.

## Validation

On a GB10 (DGX Spark), `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` at 92044241a with this branch's files mounted over it:

- **Tests**: `pytest tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions tests/entrypoints/generate/generative_scoring`, 51 passed (Qwen3-0.6B end to end, plus the unit tests). The unit tests also pass on the DiffusionGemma merge branch (23 passed).
- **JevBench**: the numbers above. The client is `jevbench_systemone.py` from #59299 with a `--native` flag that sends noul and score items as their own types. DiffusionGemma is NVFP4 with canvas 64, on the merge branch.

## Details

- A noul side with no description is left out of the prompt.
- A score has at most 10 levels, so that every label is one digit.
- Not covered in CI: DiffusionGemma, to keep a 26B checkpoint out of CI.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Accept each connection on the least loaded API worker
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With `--api-server-count N > 1`, accept each new connection on the API worker with the fewest open connections, so requests are spread evenly across workers. Part of RFC #57479. This is an alternative to #58278 (SO_REUSEPORT listeners, and the accept-pacing rewrite on that branch) and builds on its accept loop.

## Claims

- Connections are spread evenly across API workers in bursts, when they arrive one at a time, and under overload. On main, one worker often takes most of a burst.
- RL `pause(mode="abort")` on GB200, DP2, 8 API servers: abort → all response bodies received goes from **40.0 s on main to 21.5 s** (Ao's accept pacing: 26.6 s; SO_REUSEPORT: 29.8 s).
- Ordinary serving with many short requests (Qwen3-0.6B, output length 1): **+43–85% requests/s** and lower TTFT than main, because on main a client's keep-alive pool lands on a few workers.
- A single API server is unchanged, and no new flags are added.

## Validation

**GPU: RL abort cycle.** GB200, Qwen3-0.6B, `--data-parallel-size 2 --api-server-count 8`, Python frontend.
- Workload: 128 concurrent non-streaming `/inference/v1/generate` requests, top-64 logprobs, `max_tokens` 32768; `POST /pause?mode=abort` after 25 s (about 670k aborted tokens, 2.5 GB of response bodies).
- Setup: the whole server is pinned to the GPUs' CPU socket (`taskset -c 70-139`). Without pinning, a worker that the scheduler moves between sockets mid-render adds 3–6 s of noise to any variant.
- Runs: 3 per variant in alternating order. All 128 responses were valid in every run. Connections per worker were counted with psutil just before the pause.

| variant | connections per worker (busiest … idlest) | abort → all bodies received | median |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 31–34 … 5–8 | 39.2, 40.0, 43.0 s | 40.0 s |
| #58278 as reviewed (SO_REUSEPORT per worker) | 22–24 … 6–11 | 29.8, 28.1, 30.5 s | 29.8 s |
| accept one, then pause 1 ms (aoshen02 49dd8af1f5) | 19–20 … 12 | 26.6, 26.7, 24.3 s | 26.6 s |
| **this PR** | **16 on every worker, every run** | **21.4, 21.5, 21.7 s** | **21.5 s** |

Python workers render responses one at a time, so the busiest worker sets the tail. With this PR, all 8 workers finish within 0.9 s of each other.

**Short-request throughput** (requested in review). `vllm bench serve`, Qwen3-0.6B, random dataset, input 32 / output 1 tokens, `--ignore-eos --request-rate inf`, 30,000 requests per run after a 2,000-request warmup. Server pinned to the GPUs' CPU socket. 3 server starts per variant in alternating order; the PR is b9cae8206f and main is its base, 0f112d1800. All 36 runs had 0 failed requests.

| config | concurrency | main req/s (3 runs) | this PR req/s (3 runs) | change (median) | mean / p99 TTFT, main → PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP2, 8 API servers | 64 | 1156, 1101, 1010 | 2042, 2041, 2085 | +85% | 57/81 → 30/39 ms |
| | 256 | 1625, 1556, 1573 | 2300, 2290, 2324 | +46% | 160/693 → 100/156 ms |
| | 1024 | 1446, 1462, 1493 | 2081, 2097, 2164 | +43% | 685/5014 → 427/673 ms |
| DP1, 4 API servers | 64 | 965, 975, 1198 | 1476, 1478, 1418 | +51% | 65/86 → 42/60 ms |
| | 256 | 1467, 1449, 1517 | 2163, 2220, 2169 | +48% | 171/308 → 110/200 ms |
| | 1024 | 1415, 1398, 1423 | 2169, 2113, 2139 | +51% | 703/1675 → 427/808 ms |

Why: the benchmark client opens its keep-alive pool in a burst, so on main a few workers take every connection. In a separate run of DP2 × 8 API servers at concurrency 64, connections per worker were [48, 15, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0] on main and 8 on each worker with this PR. Both variants are API-server-bound at this request size, so idle workers mean lost throughput.

<details>
<summary>CPU benchmark: connection distribution under different arrival patterns</summary>

Setup:
- 8 worker processes running vLLM's `NoSignalServer` on uvloop over one shared socket, exactly as `APIServerProcessManager` starts them, with a stub ASGI app.
- Each request waits for a hold time, then blocks the event loop for a render time.
- 5 runs each. Each cell shows the busiest worker's connection count against the fair share, then the tail after the last arrival.

| scenario | main | SO_REUSEPORT | accept pacing | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 256 at once, 50 ms render | 34–245 / 32, 10.6 s | 37–45, 2.07 s | 33–35, 1.71 s | 32, 1.62 s |
| 2000 at once, 5 ms render | 488–1850 / 250, 9.0 s | 263–287, 1.48 s | 254–262, 1.39 s | 250, 1.37 s |
| 512 over 2 s, 50 ms render (overloaded) | 148–193 / 64, 7.5 s | 74–78, 2.67 s | 99–146, 4.3 s | 65–74, 2.33 s |
| 500 over 5 s, 50 ms render (~60% CPU) | — | 70–80 / 63, 0.74 s | 78–108, 1.75 s | 68–70, 0.34 s |
| 5000 at once, no work (accept throughput) | 0.83 s | 0.49 s | 0.69 s | 0.55 s |

</details>

**Tests:** `tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_balanced_accepts.py` (new) checks:
- keep-alive requests are served on both asyncio and uvloop;
- a failed TLS handshake doesn't stop the accept loop;
- a busier worker still accepts when the least-loaded worker never does;
- 4 real worker processes × 400 connections, in a burst and spread over 1 s, end up within 1.25× of the fair share.

```
pytest tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_balanced_accepts.py \
       tests/entrypoints/launchers/api_server/ \
       tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_shutdown.py
```
Result: 28 passed on GB200, including the real multi-API-server shutdown tests. `pre-commit` (including the manual-stage mypy) is clean. CI already runs the new file through the `pytest entrypoints/launchers` step.

## Details

**Root cause.** All API workers inherit one listening socket. The event loop's own server accepts every queued connection on each wakeup, so whichever worker wakes first takes the whole burst. Connections that arrive one at a time tend to go to the most recently active worker.

**Design.**
- `APIServerProcessManager` shares one `RawArray("i")` slot per worker. This is the same mechanism as the existing `mp_admission_counters`.
- Each worker serves the shared socket with its own accept loop, instead of starting an asyncio server through uvicorn.
- When the socket becomes readable, a worker refreshes its own open-connection count and accepts only if it is the least loaded.
- Otherwise it rechecks every 1 ms, up to 5 times, then accepts anyway. That way a least-loaded worker that is blocked mid-render can't stall new connections.
- Accepted sockets go through uvicorn's own protocol via `loop.connect_accepted_socket`, each in its own task, so TLS handshakes don't hold up the accept loop. On shutdown, pending accepts and handshakes are cancelled; uvicorn already drains open connections.
- Slots start at INT32_MAX, so a worker that hasn't started is never chosen.

**Why not #58278.**
- SO_REUSEPORT gives each worker its own listener, and the kernel assigns connections by hash. That's random, and it clumps: about 25% over the fair share in bursts, and the 29.8 s tail above.
- Accept pacing (accept one connection, then pause 1 ms) balances bursts. With staggered arrivals the same worker keeps getting woken first, so some workers get no connections (99–146 on one worker against a fair share of 64 in the overloaded CPU case).

**Trade-offs.**
- Balancing has a cost: when every worker is busy rendering, short requests such as `/health` wait behind a render on whichever worker accepts them. In a mixed benchmark (the ~60% CPU case above plus `/health` polled at 100/s), `/health` p99 is about 50–100 ms with this PR, against under 1 ms with main or accept pacing, which leave some workers idle. SO_REUSEPORT is 0.6–1.9 s. When the CPU is overloaded, every balanced scheme sits around 1.5 s. A 20 ms recheck window doubled this cost for little extra balance, which is why the window is 5 ms. Faster rendering reduces both sides of this trade-off.
- It balances connections, not requests: a keep-alive client stays on its worker, as with any accept-level scheme.
- Every idle worker still wakes for each new connection, as on main.

## Claims

- `tool_choice="required"` and named tool choice with `--tool-call-parser longcat` now return parsed `tool_calls` instead of raw tag text in `content`.
- The Hermes structural tag output is unchanged.

Unit test `test_longcat_forced_tool_choice_round_trips_native_tags` in `tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py` builds the forced grammar for the LongCat parser and checks that output in LongCat's native tags is accepted. commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix InternLM2 tool parser dropping characters from streamed arguments
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #60348. If a stream chunk ended inside a JSON string, `Internlm2ToolParser` dropped the closing `"` and the final `}` from the streamed tool-call arguments. The parser now computes the argument delta from the text it has already sent to the client.

## Claims

- For the chunks `{"location": "Beijing` + `", "days": 3}}<|action_end|>`, the streamed arguments were `{"location": "Beijing, "days": 3`, which is invalid JSON. They are now `{"location": "Beijing", "days": 3}`.
- A sweep over string and structure payloads, cut at many chunk boundaries, found no stream that got worse. It found 6,649 streams that were wrong before and are right now.
- The change is in one branch of `Internlm2ToolParser.extract_tool_calls_streaming`. It adds the regression test `test_streaming_arguments_match_final_arguments`, which fails on the old code.
- Not fixed: number literals that `json.dumps` writes differently from the model's text (see Details).

## Validation

Reproducer: the script below calls the parser directly. It needs no server and no model weights. Run it with `python -P repro.py`. The issue's attached script was not available, so this script was written from the issue's description. Its failing output matches the wrong value given in the issue.

Environment: 1× NVIDIA B200, vLLM commit `43b4aaea3e40e20ef53ce2bfecfa1b72060bf2b5`, with and without this patch. The bug is in pure Python, so the GPU is not used. The bug was also reproduced on the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image at the same commit.

<details>
<summary>repro.py (docstring and comments shortened, code as run)</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reproduce vllm#60348: Internlm2ToolParser drops characters from streaming args."""

import sys


class MockTokenizer:
    pass


def run_chunks(chunks, label):
    from vllm.tool_parsers.internlm2_tool_parser import Internlm2ToolParser

    class MockRequest:
        tools = []
        tool_choice = "auto"

    parser = Internlm2ToolParser(MockTokenizer())
    request = MockRequest()

    collected_args = []
    previous_text = ""

    for i, chunk in enumerate(chunks):
        current_text = previous_text + chunk
        delta_text = chunk

        result = parser.extract_tool_calls_streaming(
            previous_text=previous_text,
            current_text=current_text,
            delta_text=delta_text,
            previous_token_ids=[],
            current_token_ids=[],
            delta_token_ids=[],
            request=request,
        )

        if result and result.tool_calls:
            for tc in result.tool_calls:
                if tc.function:
                    # function is a DeltaFunctionCall pydantic model
                    fn = tc.function
                    args = fn.arguments if hasattr(fn, "arguments") else fn.get("arguments")
                    if args:
                        print(f"  chunk {i} arg delta: {repr(args)}")
                        collected_args.append(args)

        previous_text = current_text

    remaining = parser.get_remaining_unstreamed_args()
    if remaining:
        print(f"  get_remaining_unstreamed_args: {repr(remaining)}")
        collected_args.append(remaining)

    result = "".join(collected_args)
    expected = '{"location": "Beijing", "days": 3}'
    status = "PASS" if result == expected else "FAIL"
    print(f"  concatenated: {repr(result)}")
    print(f"  expected:     {repr(expected)}")
    print(f"  {status}")
    return result


# The full InternLM2 model output for a weather tool call.
FULL_TEXT = (
    '<|action_start|><|plugin|>\n'
    '{"name": "get_weather", "parameters": {"location": "Beijing", "days": 3}}\n'
    '<|action_end|>'
)

# chunk_a: ends right before the parameters value (name parseable, args not yet)
chunk_a = '<|action_start|><|plugin|>\n{"name": "get_weather", "parameters": '

# --- Failing split: chunk boundary falls BEFORE the closing " of "Beijing" ---
chunk_b_bad = '{"location": "Beijing'
chunk_c_bad = '", "days": 3}}\n<|action_end|>'

print("=== Failing split (chunk boundary before closing \" of Beijing) ===")
run_chunks([chunk_a, chunk_b_bad, chunk_c_bad], "failing")

print()

# --- Good split: chunk boundary falls AFTER the closing " of "Beijing" ---
chunk_b_good = '{"location": "Beijing"'
chunk_c_good = ', "days": 3}}\n<|action_end|>'

print("=== Good split (chunk boundary after closing \" of Beijing) ===")
run_chunks([chunk_a, chunk_b_good, chunk_c_good], "good")
```

</details>

Before, at `43b4aaea3`: 1 run, failed 1 of 1.

```
=== Failing split (chunk boundary before closing " of Beijing) ===
  chunk 1 arg delta: '{"location": "Beijing'
  chunk 2 arg delta: ', "days": 3'
  concatenated: '{"location": "Beijing, "days": 3'
  expected:     '{"location": "Beijing", "days": 3}'
  FAIL

=== Good split (chunk boundary after closing " of Beijing) ===
  chunk 1 arg delta: '{"location": "Beijing"'
  chunk 2 arg delta: ', "days": 3'
  get_remaining_unstreamed_args: '}'
  concatenated: '{"location": "Beijing", "days": 3}'
  expected:     '{"location": "Beijing", "days": 3}'
  PASS
```

After, with this PR: 2 runs, passed 2 of 2, with the same output both times. The real `"` now arrives with the next chunk. The `}` is sent once the JSON is complete, so `get_remaining_unstreamed_args()` has nothing left to add.

```
=== Failing split (chunk boundary before closing " of Beijing) ===
  chunk 1 arg delta: '{"location": "Beijing'
  chunk 2 arg delta: '", "days": 3}'
  concatenated: '{"location": "Beijing", "days": 3}'
  expected:     '{"location": "Beijing", "days": 3}'
  PASS

=== Good split (chunk boundary after closing " of Beijing) ===
  chunk 1 arg delta: '{"location": "Beijing"'
  chunk 2 arg delta: ', "days": 3}'
  concatenated: '{"location": "Beijing", "days": 3}'
  expected:     '{"location": "Beijing", "days": 3}'
  PASS
```

Tests:

- `pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_internlm2_tool_parser.py` with this PR: `12 passed, 8 xfailed`. The 8 xfails were already marked in the file.
- The new test with the original parser: `2 failed`. The streamed arguments were `{"location": "Beijing, "days": 3` (`split_inside_string`) and `{"Beijing, "days": 3` (`char_by_char`).
- `pre-commit run --files` on both changed files: all hooks passed.

Chunk-boundary sweep (scratch script, not part of this PR): 5 payloads. They were the issue's example, escaped quotes with `}` and `]` inside strings, non-ASCII and emoji with `\n` and `\\`, empty string/array/object with a list of objects, and a string with a comma. Each payload was cut at every 2-way split, at every 3-way split inside the arguments, and one character at a time, for 13,887 streams in total. The original parser got 7,158 right and the patched parser got 13,807 right. No stream went from right to wrong. The 80 streams that are still wrong all cut inside the `<|action_start|>` tag, so the parser never sees a tool call. That code is not changed here, and a real tokenizer emits the tag as one token.

Not run: an end-to-end streaming request through the server (the `internlm` config in `tests/tool_use/utils.py`). The `internlm2_5-7b-chat` weights were not available.

## Details

Root cause: `partial_json_parser` closes every open string, array and object. So for the raw text `{"location": "Beijing`, `json.dumps` of the parsed arguments gives `{"location": "Beijing"}`. The trailing `"}` is synthetic, because the model has not produced it yet. When the arguments first appear, the parser correctly sends only `{"location": "Beijing`. On the next chunk, the branch where both the previous and the current parse have arguments computed the delta with `extract_intermediate_diff(cur_args_json, prev_args_json)`. That treats `prev_args_json` as text the client already has. But `prev_args_json` contains the synthetic `"`, which was never sent, so the real `"` in the next chunk counted as already sent and was dropped. The delta never looked at what was really streamed. After that, the streamed text is no longer a prefix of the final arguments, so `get_remaining_unstreamed_args()` returns `""` and the final `}` is lost too. This is a consequence of the first problem, not a second bug. The first-arguments branch was correct and is unchanged.

Fix: the delta now starts from `sent = len(self.streamed_args_for_tool[self.current_tool_id])`.

- If the tool-call JSON is complete, send `cur_args_json[sent:]`.
- If the two parses differ, send their common prefix minus `sent`. Synthetic closers sit at the end of a serialization and change when real text arrives, so for strings and structure the common prefix holds only real text.
- If the two parses are equal, send `""`. The old code also sent an empty delta here.

`llama_tool_parser.py` and `granite_20b_fc_tool_parser.py` already use this scheme. The import changes from `extract_intermediate_diff` to `find_common_prefix`. `extract_intermediate_diff` stays in `utils.py` because `jamba_tool_parser.py` still uses it.

Limitations:

- The parser still streams `json.dumps` of the partial parse. The issue suggests streaming slices of the raw text, and this PR does not do that. So number literals that `json.dumps` writes differently can still go wrong for some splits. For `1E-3` (final `0.001`), 335 splits were wrong before and 23 after. For `0.00001` (final `1e-05`), 152 were wrong before and 37 after. Both "after" counts include 16 cuts inside the `<|action_start|>` tag. No split went from right to wrong, but the failure looks different now. For the chunks `"x": 1` + `E-3, "y": "z"}}...`, the old code sent `{"x": 10.001, "y": "z"`, which is invalid JSON. The new code sends `{"x": 1.001, "y": "z"}`, which is valid JSON with a wrong value. The llama and granite-20b-fc parsers have the same limit.
- `jamba_tool_parser.py` has the same `extract_intermediate_diff(cur_args_json, prev_args_json)` branch and may have the same bug. It is not changed here.

commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Streamed `/v1/completions` logprobs return wrong `text_offset` values when `stop` strings are set. Non-streaming is correct.

## Claims

- Streamed `text_offset` now matches the non-streaming response for the same output.

## Validation

- New `tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_text_offset.py`: fails on main (`[0, 2, 5] != [0, 3, 6]`), passes with the fix.
- Real `OutputProcessor` and detokenizer with the gpt2 tokenizer, `stop=["\n\n", "STOPNOW"]`, fed into the stream generator: on main 15 tokens sit at the wrong offset; with the fix none do, and offsets equal the non-streaming ones.
- `pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/` (server-free tests) and `pre-commit run` on the changed files pass.

## Details

With stop strings, the detokenizer holds back up to `len(longest stop) - 1` characters until it can rule out a match, but logprobs for those tokens go out immediately. The stream advanced its offset by the emitted `delta_text`, so every later offset fell short. It now advances by the reported token lengths, as the non-streaming path does (keeps the #47815 echo fix). Not a duplicate: #47815 fixed the echo case only; no open PR touches this. The Rust frontend was not checked.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Carry reasoning controls over gRPC
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Carry thinking-token budgets and per-request engine reasoning-gate inputs through the Rust gRPC `Generate` and `GenerateStream` APIs. External frontends can preserve engine-managed structured-output gating while migrating to full-output grammars.

## Claims

- Group optional `reasoning_ended` and effective `chat_template_kwargs` in `GenerateRequest.engine_reasoning_gate`, preserving omitted versus explicit `false`.
- Keep the internal `ReasoningParserKwargs` representation typed and unchanged.
- Forward `StoppingCriteria.thinking_token_budget`, including zero and the existing disabled-budget semantics.

## Validation

From `rust/`:

```sh
cargo test --locked -p vllm-server -p vllm-text -p vllm-chat -p vllm-llm -p vllm-engine-core-client --lib -- --quiet
cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

1,048 tests passed; one existing text test is ignored. The reasoning-gate regression exercises protobuf serialization, gRPC conversion, and text-to-engine lowering for unary and streaming requests, including absent/empty gates, explicit booleans, template kwargs, and budget presence. The existing server suite also exercises real gRPC transport with a mock engine-core.

Scoped pre-commit checks and `cargo publish --manifest-path rust/proto/Cargo.toml --locked --dry-run` passed. No real-model/GPU evaluation has been performed; validation establishes request propagation, not model-output quality.

## Details

The engine-core request and shared text layer already support these controls, but the gRPC schema and converter could not carry them. The nested `EngineReasoningGate` is transitional: it applies when the engine runs its own reasoning parser and the constraint covers only post-reasoning output. Full-output grammars enforced from the first generated token are the preferred direction, and grouping these controls makes their eventual deprecation explicit.

This extends the gRPC interface and complements the HTTP generate work in #60062. Output parsing remains the caller's responsibility.

The protobuf fields are additive, and `vllm-proto` is bumped to 0.5.0. Old servers ignore the new fields, so clients relying on them require an updated server; no capability-negotiation flag is added.

Downstream integration: https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/15550. Independent generation-controls and cache-usage changes: #59837.

commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Add a score template for [zerank-2](https://huggingface.co/zeroentropy/zerank-2-reranker) (ZeroEntropy, Qwen3-4B based, Apache 2.0), next to the existing Qwen3 / mxbai / nemotron templates.

- `examples/pooling/score/template/zerank2.jinja`: query in the system turn, document in the user turn, assistant suffix emitted unconditionally (score templates are rendered without `add_generation_prompt`, and zerank-2's own `chat_template.jinja` only emits the suffix when it is set, see #60409). Supports the `instruction` request field; without it, the prompt is exactly the official one.
- `using_template_online.py` / `using_template_offline.py`: add `polaria-tech/zerank-2-reranker-vllm`, a `Qwen3ForSequenceClassification` conversion of zerank-2 (single `Yes` token, head scaled by 1/5 so the default sigmoid returns zerank-2's calibrated `sigmoid(logit / 5)`).
- `docs/models/pooling_models/scoring.md`: list the model and template.

Docs and examples only, no code change.

## Test Plan

Parity against the official `CrossEncoder("zeroentropy/zerank-2-reranker").predict()`, with an fp32 ground truth, on vLLM 0.29.0 and 0.31.0 (H100, bf16, `--chat-template` with this template): 47 pairs from 19 to 38k tokens, mixed lengths per batch.

## Test Result

- Prompt token ids identical to the official path on 47/47 pairs.
- Max deviation from fp32: 0.095–0.136 logit for vLLM vs 0.183 for the official bf16 path itself (0-1 score: 0.0040 vs 0.0053).
- Without the template: mean error 11.4 logit; with zerank-2's own `chat_template.jinja`: 9.9.

Method and scripts: https://github.com/polaria-tech/zerank-2-reranker-vllm/blob/main/NOTES.md

Happy to add an MTEB test under `tests/models/language/pooling_mteb_test/` if you'd like one for this model.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Multimodal] Sort multimodal encoder inputs by modality
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Sort mm encoder inputs to reduce fragmented ViT calls

## Claims

**+6.5% req/s gain (MRV2), +8.2% req/s gain (MRV1)** on Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct on MI350X GPU

## Validation

Ran a vllm benchmark on Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct \
  --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-model-len 8192 \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1, "video": 1}' \
  --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 --no-enable-prefix-caching
```

After warmup requests, tested with 2000 random requests

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct \
  --dataset-name random-mm --num-prompts 2000 --max-concurrency 64 \
  --random-input-len 64 --random-output-len 1 \
  --random-mm-base-items-per-request 1 --random-mm-num-mm-items-range-ratio 0 \
  --random-mm-limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1, "video": 1}' \
  --random-mm-bucket-config '{(448, 448, 1): 0.2, (224, 224, 16): 0.8}'
```

**Results** (throughput in req/s, mean ± std over 7 runs; TTFT averaged over runs):

| Runner | Branch | Throughput | Mean TTFT | Median TTFT | P99 TTFT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MRV2 | main | 74.13 ± 2.34 | 852 ms | 821 ms | 1462 ms |
| MRV2 | PR | **78.92 ± 2.23 (+6.5%)** | 799 ms | 778 ms | 1332 ms |
| V1 | main | 73.94 ± 2.45 | 855 ms | 816 ms | 1506 ms |
| V1 | PR | **80.01 ± 1.45 (+8.2%)** | 790 ms | 760 ms | 1330 ms |

<details><summary>Per-run throughput (req/s)</summary>

- MRV2 main: 72.27, 76.56, 73.67, 75.14, 70.05, 76.39, 74.82
- MRV2 PR: 76.56, 75.81, 80.77, 81.57, 78.53, 78.36, 80.82
- V1 main: 76.49, 75.76, 70.96, 70.18, 74.29, 75.61, 74.27
- V1 PR: 81.01, 78.73, 78.64, 81.94, 78.24, 80.92, 80.62

</details>

**Correctness check**:

Prepared 192 samples of mm inputs (1 out of 6 colors) and asked the model 'what is the color'. 192/192 correct for both MRV1 and MRV2

<details><summary>Test snippet</summary>

```python
import argparse

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

COLORS = {
    "red": (220, 20, 20),
    "green": (20, 180, 20),
    "blue": (20, 20, 220),
    "yellow": (240, 230, 20),
    "black": (10, 10, 10),
    "white": (245, 245, 245),
}
PROMPT = (
    "<|im_start|>user\n<|vision_start|><|{pad}|><|vision_end|>"
    "What is the main color of this {modality}? Answer with one word.<|im_end|>\n"
    "<|im_start|>assistant\n"
)
NUM_FRAMES = 16
VIDEO_METADATA = {
    "total_num_frames": NUM_FRAMES,
    "fps": 2.0,
    "duration": NUM_FRAMES / 2.0,
    "video_backend": "opencv",
    "frames_indices": list(range(NUM_FRAMES)),
    "do_sample_frames": False,
}


def solid_color(rng: np.random.Generator, color: str, shape: tuple) -> np.ndarray:
    # Per-item noise keeps every mm_hash unique, so cache sharing cannot hide
    # a misrouted encoder output.
    pixels = np.array(COLORS[color]) + rng.integers(-8, 9, shape)
    return np.clip(pixels, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)


def make_requests(num_requests: int, image_ratio: float, seed: int):
    """Randomly interleaved image/video requests and their (color, modality)."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    requests, labels = [], []
    for _ in range(num_requests):
        color = list(COLORS)[rng.integers(len(COLORS))]
        if rng.random() < image_ratio:
            image = Image.fromarray(solid_color(rng, color, (448, 448, 3)))
            mm_data = {"image": image}
            prompt = PROMPT.format(pad="image_pad", modality="image")
            modality = "image"
        else:
            video = solid_color(rng, color, (NUM_FRAMES, 224, 224, 3))
            mm_data = {"video": (video, VIDEO_METADATA)}
            prompt = PROMPT.format(pad="video_pad", modality="video")
            modality = "video"
        requests.append({"prompt": prompt, "multi_modal_data": mm_data})
        labels.append((color, modality))
    return requests, labels


def score(labels, answers) -> dict:
    """Accuracy per modality, plus the failing cases."""
    correct = [color in answer for (color, _), answer in zip(labels, answers)]
    result = {
        m: f"{sum(c for c, (_, mod) in zip(correct, labels) if mod == m)}"
        f"/{sum(mod == m for _, mod in labels)}"
        for m in ("image", "video")
    }
    result["total"] = f"{sum(correct)}/{len(correct)}"
    result["wrong"] = [
        (i, labels[i], answers[i]) for i, ok in enumerate(correct) if not ok
    ]
    return result


def main(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    requests, labels = make_requests(args.num_requests, args.image_ratio, args.seed)
    # Same engine settings as the serving benchmark, so each step encodes a
    # modality-interleaved batch.
    llm = LLM(
        "Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct",
        max_num_seqs=64,
        max_num_batched_tokens=16384,
        max_model_len=8192,
        limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1, "video": 1},
        mm_processor_cache_gb=0,
        enable_prefix_caching=False,
        seed=args.seed,
    )
    outputs = llm.generate(requests, SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=4))
    answers = [o.outputs[0].text.strip().lower() for o in outputs]
    print(score(labels, answers))
```

</details>

## Details

When images and videos are scheduled in the same step, the encoder gets split into many small calls. So, sort modalities are sorted before to make each modalities run as one batch.

commits.pr_title: [BugFix][DiffusionGemma][CPU] Copy async output snapshots instead of aliasing reused buffers
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #59828

## Claims

With async scheduling, the V2 model runner snapshots each step's sampled tokens and counts with `async_copy_to_np()`. It reads them after the next step starts. On GPU, `.to("cpu")` copies into new memory. On CPU it returns the same tensor, and the snapshot aliases the sampler's buffers. DiffusionGemma reuses those buffers on every step, and the next step overwrites the snapshot before it is read.

This is latent on `main`. CPU forces sync scheduling, which reads each output before the next step runs. I found it while testing DiffusionGemma structured reads on CPU with async scheduling enabled, after https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59107. Every read returned a phantom first token, overwritten tokens and one logprob row too few.

### Changes in this PR

- `async_copy_to_np()` passes `copy=True`. A CPU snapshot now owns its memory. GPU behavior does not change. The device-to-host copy already allocates.
- Add a regression test to `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py`, next to the other V2 model runner tests, instead of a new file. It snapshots a CPU tensor, overwrites the tensor and checks that the snapshot keeps its values.

I checked the other snapshots in `AsyncOutput`. Logprobs, sampling masks and prompt logprobs also alias on CPU. They are safe because their producers allocate new tensors on every step. I left them as is.

No open issue or PR covers this. I searched for `async_copy_to_np`, CPU async aliasing and overwritten sampled tokens. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58082 edits the code next to `async_copy_to_np()` but does not change it.

I used Claude Code to help with this PR. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests below.

## Validation

Hardware: 22 vCPU Intel Xeon Platinum 8481C, Ubuntu 22.04, PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu. vLLM built from source for CPU at e006d761a5, with the real `google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it` checkpoint in BF16. Unit tests also on macOS (Apple Silicon).

**Unit tests:**

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py
```

**End to end:**

1. Sync path, the default on CPU. Run greedy generation with `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` and a DiffusionGemma structured read (32-token canvas on a 64-token server). Run on `main`, with this PR, and on `main` again for the noise floor. Compare tokens, logprobs and throughput.
2. Async path. Enable async scheduling on CPU with a local change to `CpuPlatform.check_and_update_config()`. Send the same DiffusionGemma read 10 times with a batch of 1 and 10 times with a batch of 4. Compare each read with sync.

## Test Result

Before (`main`, async on CPU), the read's tokens are overwritten. The issue has the details and the `collect_env.py` output.

```text
sync   tokens[:8] [45518, 45518, 107, 148436, 148436, 236787, 11262, 1]   logprob rows 32
async  tokens[:8] [45518, 1, 1, 1, 1, 148436, 236787, 11262]              logprob rows 31
```

After:

- Unit tests: 90 passed. The new test fails on `main` with `assert [1, 1, 1, 1] == [0, 0, 0, 0]`.
- Async: 50/50 reads match sync, up from 0/50. No snapshot changes before it is read, even with the reader delayed by 50 ms.
- Sync: [layer 3 results: tokens and logprobs before and after for both models, throughput against the noise floor]

## Details

On CPU, .to("cpu") returns the same tensor, and with async scheduling the next step overwrites the sampled-token snapshot before it is read. That corrupted every DiffusionGemma read I tested (linked in the issue).

This PR copies in `async_copy_to_np()`, the one place sampler outputs cross the async boundary. GPU behavior does not change. CPU pays one small copy per step. main is unaffected today because CPU forces sync scheduling. Logprob snapshots still alias but stay safe because their producers allocate new tensors.

commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Reject fused 3D MoE LoRA weights on a 2D wrapper when the required format settings are missing, with an error naming both settings.

Addresses the actionable-error follow-up in item 4 of #59799; complements #59801.

## Claims

- Detect this incompatible layout before adapter registration and activation.
- Explain how to enable `enable_mixed_moe_lora_format` and set `is_3d_lora_weight`.
- Check during worker loading before replacing or evicting a cached adapter.

## Validation

Validated on one NVIDIA A10G (AWS g5.2xlarge), FP16, using a tiny random Qwen3-MoE model and a PEFT 0.21.2 adapter, based on commit `6f75cc7d5d1b5adfb399cbf79a8231ae66844fcf`.

These results cover the patch committed as `2f8c900063f3`, before the subsequent merge of `main` into this branch. They are not CI results for the updated PR head.

- `python -m pytest tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py -v`: **28 passed**, including eight new cases.
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/lora/model_manager.py vllm/lora/worker_manager.py tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py docs/features/lora.md`: all applicable hooks passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

| Full-engine case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Original reproducer, missing both settings | Bare assertion replaced by a descriptive worker `ValueError`; generation still ends with `EngineDeadError`. |
| Original reproducer, both settings enabled | Generates `[190, 737, 34, 78]`, matching the baseline control. |
| Dynamic `add_lora`, each of the three missing-flag combinations | Returns the actionable error; generation continues afterward. |
| Dynamic rejection with a valid adapter already filling the cache | Valid adapter ID remains registered; deterministic generation is unchanged. |

The original generation reproducer is in #59799; these runs use FP16 on the
A10G. The dynamic-loading harness below is self-contained:

```sh
VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn python validate_59799.py
VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn python validate_59799.py --mixed
```

Both commands complete successfully. New unit cases run in the existing LoRA CI
job. Multi-GPU behavior and HTTP serving were not tested.

This is a loading/activation smoke test, not a model-quality evaluation. The change does not alter LoRA scaling, conversion or kernels.

<details>
<summary>Dynamic-loading validation harness (save as validate_59799.py)</summary>

```python
"""Validate dynamic loading errors and continued generation on a CUDA engine."""
import argparse
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile
import torch
from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, Qwen3MoeConfig
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
from vllm.inputs import TokensPrompt
from vllm.lora.request import LoRARequest


def make_checkpoint(directory):
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    config = Qwen3MoeConfig(
        vocab_size=1024, hidden_size=256, intermediate_size=512,
        moe_intermediate_size=128, num_hidden_layers=2,
        num_attention_heads=4, num_key_value_heads=2, head_dim=64,
        num_experts=8, num_experts_per_tok=2, tie_word_embeddings=False,
    )
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config(config, dtype=torch.float16)
    model.save_pretrained(directory / "base")
    lora = LoraConfig(
        r=16, lora_alpha=32, target_modules=[],
        target_parameters=["mlp.experts.gate_up_proj", "mlp.experts.down_proj"],
    )
    get_peft_model(model, lora).save_pretrained(directory / "lora")

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--mixed", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        directory = Path(tmp)
        make_checkpoint(directory)
        llm = LLM(str(directory / "base"), skip_tokenizer_init=True,
                  dtype="float16", enable_lora=True, max_lora_rank=16,
                  max_cpu_loras=1, max_loras=1, max_model_len=256,
                  gpu_memory_utilization=0.3, enforce_eager=True,
                  enable_mixed_moe_lora_format=args.mixed)
        prompt = TokensPrompt(prompt_token_ids=list(range(10, 40)))
        params = SamplingParams(max_tokens=4, temperature=0, detokenize=False)
        engine = llm.llm_engine
        good = LoRARequest("good", 1, str(directory / "lora"), is_3d_lora_weight=True)
        if args.mixed:
            assert engine.add_lora(good)
            before = llm.generate(prompt, params, lora_request=good)[0].outputs[0].token_ids
            expected_ids = {1}
        else:
            before = llm.generate(prompt, params)[0].outputs[0].token_ids
            expected_ids = set()
        declarations = [False] if args.mixed else [False, True]
        for declared in declarations:
            bad = LoRARequest("bad", 2, str(directory / "lora"), is_3d_lora_weight=declared)
            try:
                engine.add_lora(bad)
            except Exception as exc:
                message = str(exc)
                assert "enable_mixed_moe_lora_format=True" in message, message
                assert "is_3d_lora_weight=True" in message, message
                print("EXPECTED REJECTION:", type(exc).__name__, message, flush=True)
            else:
                raise AssertionError("Incompatible adapter was accepted")
            actual_ids = engine.list_loras()
            print("REGISTERED ADAPTERS:", repr(actual_ids), flush=True)
            assert set(actual_ids) == expected_ids, actual_ids
            after = llm.generate(prompt, params, lora_request=good if args.mixed else None)[0].outputs[0].token_ids
            assert after == before, (before, after)
            print("PASS: engine remains usable; adapters", expected_ids, "tokens", after, flush=True)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

## Details

Without both format settings, fused expert tensors reach `FusedMoEWithLoRA.set_lora`, which expects packed lists and raises a bare assertion. The validator checks actual loaded weights and wrapper type, preserving native 3D wrappers and the supported mixed-format conversion path. Per-expert and attention-only adapters are not rejected.

The check runs on adapter loading, not each token. It is deliberately limited to this layout mismatch; it does not provide general adapter validation or change exception handling during generation. Lazy loading through `LLM.generate()` can still terminate the engine, now with actionable configuration guidance in the worker error.

No duplication: #59801 handles per-module scaling and rank validation and explicitly leaves this error-handling follow-up open. #52198 handles tensor orientation, and #59915 handles Inkling-specific conversion.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Fix multimodal embedding merge in Llama 4 and Mistral Large 3 EAGLE drafters
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57630.

Regression from #50417 (first released in v0.28.0): that change marked these drafters as `SupportsMultiModalEmbeddings` so the speculator started routing multimodal batches through their `embed_input_ids`, which had been an unreachable alias of `SupportsMultiModal.embed_input_ids` until then. cc @TQCB

`EagleLlama4ForCausalLM` and `EagleMistralLarge3ForCausalLM` implement `SupportsMultiModalEmbeddings` by borrowing the method object `SupportsMultiModal.embed_input_ids`. That method calls `self._embed_text_input_ids(...)` and reads `self._has_oov_mm_tokens`, both of which live on `SupportsMultiModal`, which the drafters do not inherit. Any multimodal target paired with one of these drafters fails during the first draft prefill (already in the profile run at startup):

```
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py", line 427, in _run_model
File "vllm/model_executor/models/interfaces.py", line 507, in embed_input_ids
AttributeError: 'EagleLlama4ForCausalLM' object has no attribute '_embed_text_input_ids'. Did you mean: 'embed_input_ids'?
```

Reproduced on main (bf13ecc) and present in v0.28.0 and v0.29.0 with `RedHatAI/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-quantized.w4a16` + `morgendave/EAGLE-Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct`, TP=4, `--speculative-config '{"method":"eagle","model":...,"num_speculative_tokens":3}'`, default cudagraph mode. The same aliasing exists in `EagleMistralLarge3ForCausalLM`; Model Runner V1 takes the same `embed_input_ids` path.

## Change

Replace the borrowed method with an explicit `embed_input_ids` in both drafters that embeds the draft input ids via `self.model.embed_input_ids` and merges external multimodal embeddings with `_merge_multimodal_embeddings`, the same shape `EagleMistralForCausalLM` already uses. No behavior change for text-only batches.

## Test plan

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py -v   # 21 passed (2 new)
pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/llama4_eagle.py vllm/model_executor/models/mistral_large_3_eagle.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py
```

New test `test_mm_capable_drafter_merges_multimodal_embeddings` (parametrized over both classes) checks text-only embedding and the merge of multimodal rows; it raises `AttributeError` on main.

E2E (4x NVIDIA L4, TP=4, TRITON_ATTN, `RedHatAI/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-quantized.w4a16` + `morgendave/EAGLE-Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct`, `num_speculative_tokens=3`, `max_patches=4`, 18 text + 12 image prompts, greedy, 48 new tokens):

| build | cudagraph_mode | text AL | image AL | image per-pos acceptance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main @ bf13ecc | FULL_AND_PIECEWISE | startup crash (`AttributeError: ... '_embed_text_input_ids'`) | | |
| main + this PR | FULL_AND_PIECEWISE | 2.637 (328 drafts) | 2.424 (238 drafts) | 0.710 / 0.445 / 0.269 |
| main + this PR | NONE | 2.674 (322 drafts) | 2.413 (240 drafts) | 0.708 / 0.446 / 0.258 |

Image prompts now draft with acceptance close to text prompts, i.e. the drafter is receiving the image embeddings.

commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Prevent leaked shared memory when ECCPU scheduler initialization fails with NIXL enabled. The constructor currently raises without releasing the region it has already allocated.

## Claims

- Failed NIXL setup releases the scheduler-owned mmap file, file descriptors, and mapping while preserving the original exception.

## Validation

Review validation with NIXL 1.4.1: the previous constructor test file reproduced the test-order failure (6 passed, 1 failed); importing `data.nixl` before monkeypatching fixes its cached bindings, and all 7 constructor tests pass together. The suites below were rerun after merging upstream main.

The missing-NIXL regression fails against the unchanged scheduler because the mmap file remains, and passes with this fix. A second CPU regression raises during control-transport creation after data transport setup, and checks deregistration, shared-region release, and preservation of the original exception.

```bash
uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_scheduler_nixl_ctor.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/cpu/scheduler \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/cpu/test_ec_shared_region.py -q
# 76 passed (NIXL 1.4.1 installed)

uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  -m cpu_test tests/v1/ec_connector/unit -q
# 62 passed, 350 deselected

uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python pre-commit run --files \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_scheduler_nixl_ctor.py \
  vllm/distributed/ec_transfer/ec_connector/cpu/scheduler/__init__.py
# All applicable hooks passed, including mypy and test tethering.
```


Nearby transport/session/scheduler tests also passed (95 tests):

```bash
uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_data.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_session.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_control.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_scheduler_nixl_consumer.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_scheduler_nixl_producer.py -q
```

A separate CPU check exercised `ECConnectorFactory` through `ECCPUConnector` using real `VllmConfig`/`ModelConfig` objects and a local tiny Llava configuration, without replacing the shared-memory factory. The unchanged scheduler left the file, two file descriptors, and a mapping after the missing-NIXL error; the fixed scheduler left none, with the same error. Descriptors and mappings were checked through `/proc/self/fd` and `/proc/self/maps`.

Environment: Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL, Python 3.12.14, torch 2.13.0+cpu, editable source with official v0.30.0 CPU precompiled binaries. Exact-commit CPU binaries were unavailable. NIXL 1.4.1 was installed for this review revision, and the constructor wiring test exercised real NIXL registration and ZMQ session startup. Full GPU serving and cross-process NIXL data transfer were not run; local validation covers scheduler construction and startup-failure cleanup. The new test is selected by the existing CPU EC connector job in `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`.

## Details

The region is allocated before `_setup_nixl`; if setup raises, the caller never receives a scheduler to shut down. The constructor owns failure unwinding through `shutdown()`, releasing NIXL resources before the shared region. `_setup_nixl()` propagates errors without a second cleanup handler.

Related: #56507, #56508. The related test/doc PR covers import isolation and documentation, rather than constructor cleanup. Searches for EC scheduler cleanup, NIXL initialization, and shared-memory leaks found no equivalent open PR.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex prepared the patch and this review revision, and ran the validation above. The submitting human reviewed the original patch, personally reran its 74-pass/1-skip suite, and authorized this revision to address the review. No inference-output or performance change is claimed.

commits.pr_title: [Perf] Reduce fallback decode CPU by 69% at 32K
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fallback detokenization copies the full token-string history on every decode step, even though it reads only the trailing window. This change copies the required window and keeps the caller's absolute offsets.

## Claims

- **69% lower fallback decode CPU time** at 32,768 tokens per request in the final-output replay: **7.46 s → 2.30 s**.
- Decoded text and token IDs match the baseline. Prompt initialization and offset behavior are preserved.

## Validation

The replay runs the real `SlowIncrementalDetokenizer` caller on one CPU core, with four English, Chinese, Burmese, and emoji inputs and the Pixtral Mistral tokenizer. Each version has one warmup and three timed runs per size and output mode. Times cover all four requests. No model inference runs in this benchmark.

| Tokens per request | Output | Baseline CPU median (range) | Patch CPU median (range) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8,192 | Final | 0.85 s (0.83–0.88) | 0.51 s (0.50–0.52) |
| 32,768 | Final | 7.46 s (7.34–7.62) | 2.30 s (2.26–2.33) |
| 32,768 | Streamed | 8.85 s (8.80–9.04) | 2.28 s (2.26–2.36) |

Live checks used Ministral-3-3B-Instruct-2512 on one L4. All 24 baseline/patch response pairs matched text, token IDs, finish and stop reasons, and usage. Four requests of 6,144 tokens showed no confirmed serving gain: request-time medians were 145.03 s and 145.23 s. API CPU medians were 4.64 s and 4.765 s, with overlapping ranges. The 69% claim applies to the replay above.

Tests run on both helper versions:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_detokenize.py -q -k '(gpt2 or Pixtral or long_history or prompt_window) and not logprobs_count'
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py -q
```

Each version passed **81 tokenizer tests and 94 renderer tests**. There were 91 existing skips, 660 deselected cases, and one expected failure. The added cases cover long Unicode output, the first-call prompt window, and offsets past the window. The 81 tokenizer tests passed again on both helper versions after the base update. Local pre-commit and Python 3.12 mypy checks passed. Upstream CI is enabled. Its failed steps are being checked and retried.

## Details

`prev_tokens + new_tokens` creates the full-history copy before the helper takes its decode slices. The patch starts at the earliest required offset and adjusts the slice indexes within that window. It returns the full token count as the absolute read offset and keeps the initial prompt tokens. The window can still grow when text is incomplete. Other copies in the caller remain.

This removes a full-history copy in the Python fallback helper. The open prompt-priming PRs #51281 and #57330 change the fast `DecodeStream` path. PR #46723 changes the Rust frontend. These are separate code paths.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Keep the GLM-5.3 kpool tail and Qwen4 QSA ring out of the null block
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Block id 0 is the null block. It is shared by every KV cache group and is assumed to stay zero. Since #35431, the runners mark rows that own no state with 0 in the block table, not `PAD_SLOT_ID`: dummy runs, CUDA graph capture and padding rows all carry 0. Two ring caches that address their pages through column 0 of the block table did not treat 0 as "no ring", so dummy runs wrote their rows into block 0:

- **GLM-5.3-Flash kpool tail:** `_kpool_tail_slot_mapping_kernel` maps every token to `block_table[req][0] * kpool + pos % kpool`. Its torch fallback does the same.
- **Qwen4 QSA circular ring:** `circular_qsa_slot_mapping` and `_build_qsa_metadata_kernel` map tokens to `block_table[req, 0]` and kept every block `>= 0`. The compressed QSA path already keeps dummy slots inert (`test_qsa_compressed_metadata_keeps_dummy_slots_inert`); the ring path did not.

Every scheduled request owns its ring block, so a request on the null block has none. Its tokens now map to PAD, as the generic slot mapping does. The ring writers already skip PAD slots.

This is the same pattern as #58560, which fixes the DeepSeek-V4.1 compressor ring.

## Changes

- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`: the kpool tail slot mapping (Triton and torch) emits PAD for requests on the null block.
- `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/common/qsa_cache.py`: the QSA circular ring slot mapping (torch and Triton) requires block `> 0`.
- Tests: the existing QSA circular metadata test, which runs the Triton builder, also checks a dummy batch (all-zero block table) and expects PAD. QSA tests that used block 0 as a real ring block now start real blocks at 1. This includes `_make_block_table` in the AMD pre-indexer test, which could randomly hand out block 0. For the kpool tail, the existing CPU padding test now ends with a padding request on the null block, and the existing Triton-vs-CPU test adds a mixed batch and an all-null dummy batch. Both check that the null-block request maps to PAD.

## Not a duplicate

- #58560 covers only the DeepSeek-V4.1 compressor ring.
- #57158 zeroes block 0 after capture. That does not cover DP idle-rank dummy batches during serving.
- #57169 and #59297 move the kpool tail onto `CircularBufferSpec` / the packed layout but keep its slot kernel unchanged.
- #54296 masks out-of-range block indices in the generic slot mapping kernel, which neither ring uses.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_pre_indexer_amd.py tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
```

## Test Result

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Build] Fail fast when `setup.py develop` deps aren't pip-preinstalled
commits.pr_body:
Recently hit this issue (#34073) myself when installing vLLM in editable mode in a ROCm container. This PR adds a preflight check that fails fast with an actionable error- pointing the user to run `pip install -r requirements/rocm.txt`,  instead of letting `python setup.py develop` crash deep in a C compile step.

## Purpose

`python setup.py develop` on ROCm resolves missing `install_requires` via setuptools' legacy `easy_install` path instead of pip's resolver. That path has repeatedly failed trying to compile old sdists of fast-moving C-extension packages (e.g. `aiohttp`) from source, surfacing as a cryptic compiler error instead of the real dependency problem:

```
aiohttp/_websocket.c:196:12: fatal error: longintrepr.h: No such file or directory
```

Reported in #34073. The [ROCm docs](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/getting_started/installation/gpu.rocm.inc.md) already recommend `pip install -r requirements/rocm.txt` before `python setup.py develop`, but users who skip that step still hit this confusing failure with no indication of the real cause.

## What this changes

Adds `_check_requirements_preinstalled()`, scoped to `_is_hip() and "develop" in sys.argv[1:]`. Before setuptools' resolver runs, it verifies every `requirements/rocm.txt` entry is installed and version-satisfied, raising an actionable error if not:

```
The following dependencies are missing or outdated:
  aiohttp >= 3.14.3

`python setup.py develop` cannot reliably install these itself (see
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/34073). Install them with pip
first, e.g.:
  pip install -r requirements/rocm.txt
then re-run `python setup.py develop`.
```

The check is skipped when `--no-deps` is passed: that flag makes setuptools skip `install_requires` processing entirely, so the failure this guards against can't occur. This also keeps the existing `python_only_compile.sh` ROCm CI job (which runs `setup.py develop --no-deps`) unaffected.

No other build path is touched — `bdist_wheel`, `egg_info`, and pip's isolated builds (used by `docker/Dockerfile.rocm` and CI) don't match this scoping and already install `requirements/rocm.txt` before building.

## Test Plan & Result

- `python3 -m py_compile setup.py`
- Verified all 78 flattened lines in `requirements/rocm.txt` parse via `packaging.requirements.Requirement`.
- Simulated the check against real installed packages: flags missing/outdated requirements, stays silent when satisfied, and no-ops under `--no-deps`.

No functional change for any build path except `python setup.py develop` on ROCm with unmet dependencies, which now fails fast with a clear message instead of a cryptic C compiler error.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][NIXL] Transfer the whole PLE short-conv page in disaggregated P/D
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59642 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: 0% MTP acceptance in disaggregated P/D serving with `NixlConnector`).

The NIXL worker folds every KV cache layer that reports the same base address into one region (`register_kv_caches`, `if base_addr in seen_base_addresses`). In the block-outer HMA layout every cache group places its first page at byte 0 of the shared allocation, so on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next the PLE short-conv state (`Qwen4ExpPLELayer`, a tp-replicated `MambaSpec`, page = `channels × (conv_state_len + num_spec_tokens)` = 245760 B) lands in the same region as layer-0 GDN, the layer-3 QSA ring and the layer-3 MLA indexer cache, and that region keeps the MLA page length (204800 B). The PLE descriptors built from `block_len_per_layer[_ple_region_index]` therefore transfer only 204800/245760 bytes of each PLE slot: 8534 of 10240 channels arrive on the decode worker, the rest is whatever the block held before (never zeroed: the block is exempt from zeroing because an async load is expected to overwrite it). With `num_speculative_tokens >= 2` the spec-decode short conv reads those stale columns, the layer-1 hidden state becomes NaN, the target logits are NaN and the rejection sampler rejects every draft (the generated tokens are garbage too, not just slow).

This PR records the PLE page length at registration (`_ple_block_len`) and uses it for the PLE descriptors on both sides of the transfer (`_build_mamba_local` / `_build_mamba_remote`), exchanging it through `NixlAgentMetadata.ple_block_len` (optional, backward compatible) so the existing P/D geometry check still compares PLE pages. Region discovery is unchanged: the PLE keeps sharing its region with the pages it aliases, as `test_csa_linear_registration_discovers_shared_regions` expects; only the transfer length of its pages changes.

## Test Plan

- New unit test `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_ple_region.py`: a CSA-linear-like config (MLA + GDN + ring + PLE sharing byte 0 of one block-outer tensor, PLE page larger than the MLA page); asserts the PLE descriptors cover the whole PLE page and that the page length is advertised in the handshake metadata. Before the fix the PLE descriptors carry the MLA page length.
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py` + `test_nixl_desc_geometry.py` run inside the serving image (vLLM `109b5363fc`) with the patch hot-patched: 307 passed before and after (one HF-download test deselected).
- End-to-end on GB200 (vLLM `109b5363fc` + this patch hot-patched into the image, Dynamo + `NixlConnector`, 1P/1D, `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`, MTP k=3, 200 requests of 64/64 tokens): mean acceptance length goes from 1.00 on 20/21 windows (zero accepted drafts) to 2.7–3.5 on every window, no NaN; the same configuration in aggregate mode gives ~2.1–2.4.

## Test Result

See above; details and the full investigation (per-request probes of the PLE conv state on prefill and decode, per-column comparison of the transferred slot) are in #59642.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Route by swap-row capacity, not the index-group workspace
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

HiSparse crashes when a batch has exactly `max_num_seqs * max_decode_query_len + 1` tokens. With `max_num_seqs=1` the engine fails at startup, and with `max_num_seqs=2` a 3-token prompt crashes at runtime:

```
ValueError: HiSparse swap rows exceed the configured speculative decode capacity: stop=2, capacity=1.
```

Part of #60072.

## Claims

- HiSparse now routes a batch to `swap_in` only when the batch fits the swap rows that `swap_in` consumes. Larger batches take the existing all-resident fallback.
- No performance impact: the change is a Python-side routing comparison against a fixed size. Batches up to the swap capacity take the same path as before; only the single size that crashed changes path.

## Validation

1×H200, upstream `main` 242e4213fc. Repro (tiny DeepSeek-V3.2, dummy weights):

```python
import sys
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
from vllm.config import AttentionConfig, HiSparseConfig, KVTransferConfig

llm = LLM(
    "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2", load_format="dummy",
    hf_overrides={"num_hidden_layers": 8, "hidden_size": 256, "intermediate_size": 512,
                  "num_attention_heads": 8, "num_key_value_heads": 1, "n_routed_experts": 8,
                  "num_experts_per_tok": 2, "index_topk": 128},
    max_model_len=320, block_size=64, max_num_seqs=int(sys.argv[1]),
    enable_prefix_caching=False, gpu_memory_utilization=0.3,
    kv_transfer_config=KVTransferConfig(kv_connector="HiSparseConnector", kv_role="kv_both",
                                        kv_connector_extra_config={"host_pool_gib": 1}),
    attention_config=AttentionConfig(hisparse_config=HiSparseConfig()),
)
for n in (2, 3, 200):
    llm.generate([{"prompt_token_ids": list(range(100, 100 + n))}],
                 SamplingParams(max_tokens=8, ignore_eos=True))
```

| Command | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `python repro.py 1` | Startup fails during piecewise CUDA-graph capture at size 2: `stop=2, capacity=1` | All 3 prompts complete |
| `python repro.py 2` | Startup succeeds; the 3-token prompt crashes: `stop=3, capacity=2` | All 3 prompts complete |
| 61-layer DeepSeek-V3.2 (8 experts, dummy weights), `max_num_seqs=1`, 16k context, 256 output tokens, `host_pool_gib=32` | Startup fails: `stop=2, capacity=1` | Runs; TPOT 18.4 ms over 3 reps |

Tests on this PR (each command run separately):

- `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k "hisparse or index_group"`: 40 passed. The regression case `test_hisparse_resident_prefill_uses_attention_block_stride` fails on `main` and passes with this PR.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py`: 9 passed
- `pytest tests/v1/core -k hisparse`: 72 passed
- `pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py`: 4 passed

## Details

**Root cause.** `HiSparseMLAIndexGroup.convert_logical_to_physical_topk` sends a batch to `swap_in` whenever the batch fits `physical_topk_indices`. That index-group workspace is allocated with one spare row (`max_decode_rows + 1`). `swap_in`, however, writes into the HiSparse runtime's shared swap rows, which hold exactly `min(max_num_batched_tokens, max_num_seqs * max_decode_query_len)` rows. A batch one token larger than the swap capacity therefore passes the routing check and then overflows in `_step_rows`.

With `max_num_seqs=1`, the CUDA-graph capture sizes are `[1, 2]`. The 2-token piecewise capture follows the all-resident prefill path into this conversion, so the engine fails at startup. With `max_num_seqs=2`, capture sizes `[1, 2, 4]` skip 3 tokens, so the failure only appears when a real 3-token batch arrives.

**Fix.** Route on `HiSparseRuntime.max_swap_rows`, the capacity that `swap_in` actually consumes. The non-HiSparse `SparseMLAIndexGroup` does not change.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Structured Output] Feed the token that implicitly ends reasoning to the grammar
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Structured output skipped a reasoning-end token that is also content, such as GLM's `<tool_call>` with no `</think>` before it. The grammar then forced a second `<tool_call>`, and `required`/named tool calls were lost. This PR feeds that token to the grammar, which matches what `extract_content_ids` already does. Fixes #59608.

## Claims

- For `ParserEngine`-based parsers, the grammar now consumes a reasoning-end token that `extract_content_ids` keeps as content, if the grammar accepts it. Close tags such as `</think>` are still skipped. `ReasoningParser` and legacy parsers do not change.
- On GLM-5.3-Flash, the doubled-`<tool_call>` signature went from 7/40 (`required`) and 8/40 (named) to 0/40. With MTP speculative decoding it went from 9/40 and 11/40 to 0/40.
- Under speculative decoding, a drafted `<tool_call>` cannot force the end of reasoning, and when it is the last draft the bonus row is masked from the grammar state after it.
- The same failure reproduces on Qwen3 (`qwen3` + `hermes`), and the fix removes it there too. Correct-call rates on the GLM tool-result prompt did not go up, because of a separate argument bug (see Limitations).

## Validation

### Unit tests

```
pytest tests/v1/structured_output tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py tests/parser \
  tests/reasoning tests/tool_parsers/test_glm47_moe_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_glm4_moe_tool_parser.py \
  --ignore=tests/parser/cohere
```

Result with 1 GPU visible: 6402 passed, 1 xfailed. `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` and the manual mypy-3.12 hook pass.

New tests are `test_inclusive_reasoning_end_token` and `test_end_token_committed_alone` in `tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py` (xgrammar and guidance), and `test_implicit_reasoning_end_of_parsers` (real `glm47_moe` config) in `tests/parser/engine/test_parser_engine.py`. With grammar start forced to the constraint start, 8 of the 13 new cases fail: `inclusive`, `inclusive_first`, `inclusive_last` and `no_drafts`, on both backends.

CI runs these tests through `misc.yaml`. `tests/parser/cohere` is left out because it needs the optional `cohere_melody` package.

A CPU script that drives the scheduler flow (validate drafts, bitmask, accept, next bitmask) with `<tool_call>` as the last draft, the only draft, a mid-window draft and the recovered token gives a second `<tool_call>` in all 8 stock cases and none with the fix.

### Live runs

The live runs used the first version of this PR (5805e42cfa). The current commit only restructures that code, and the unit tests and the CPU check give the same results on both versions.

GLM-5.3-Flash (`RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4`), TP4 on H100, xgrammar, the tool-result repro from the issue, 40 seeds at temperature 0.7:

```
vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  [--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}']
```

| Doubled-`<tool_call>` signatures, 40 seeds | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `required` | 7 | **0** |
| named | 8 | **0** |
| `required`, MTP | 9 | **0** |
| named, MTP | 11 | **0** |

MTP draft acceptance was 59.1% before and 58.5% after.

Qwen3 (`Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `--tool-call-parser hermes --reasoning-parser qwen3`), `logit_bias` -100 on `</think>` and +5 on `<tool_call>`, temperature 0, 3 repeats:

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.5 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes --reasoning-parser qwen3
```

| Mode | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `required` | 0/3 calls, 3/3 signatures | **3/3 calls** |
| named | 0/3 calls, 3/3 signatures | **3/3 calls** |
| `auto` (control) | 3/3 calls | 3/3 calls |

No standard tool-calling eval (such as BFCL) was run.

## Details

**Root cause.** `_get_constraint_start` returned the index after the reasoning-end token. That is right for `</think>`, which is not content. A tool-call start that ends reasoning is content, so the grammar started one token after the content did. This came in with #55223, and #48200 kept it.

**Change.**

- `ParserEngine.find_reasoning_end_offset` becomes `find_reasoning_end`, which returns `ReasoningEnd(offset, implicit)`. `implicit` is True when the end token is not the close tag, the same rule `extract_content_ids` uses.
- `StructuredOutputManager._get_constraint_start` becomes `_get_constraint_bounds`, which returns `ConstraintBounds(grammar_start, constraint_start)`. For an implicit end that the grammar accepts, the grammar starts at the end token and masking starts one token later. Otherwise both equal the old value.
- `validate_tokens`, the spec-decode loop of `grammar_bitmask` and `accept_tokens` feed the grammar from `grammar_start`. Masked rows and early returns still use `constraint_start`, so a drafted `<tool_call>` cannot force the target to end reasoning.
- The "grammar accepts it" check keeps the old skip when the grammar cannot start with that token, such as a `json_schema` response format with tools present.

**Affected parsers.** Every in-tree `ParserEngine` config whose tool-call start ends reasoning now feeds that token to the grammar: glm47_moe (and ling3), qwen3 (and mimo), nemotron_v3, granite_thinking, seed_oss, gemma4, kimi_k2, minimax_m2, deepseek_v4, deepseek_v41, plamo3, and mistral with `reasoning_encoding="special_token"`. A token counts only if the tokenizer has a single id for it. On the real DeepSeek-V4 tokenizer the DSML opener is several tokens, so deepseek_v4 does not change in practice. For plamo3 the token is the end-of-turn tag, which is normally a stop token; I expect that to be harmless but did not test it.

**Tradeoffs.**

- No measurable cost. After reasoning ends, `_get_constraint_bounds` returns before any reasoner call. Only a step with an implicit end token runs one extra single-token `validate_tokens` on the CPU. There is no CPU/GPU sync.

**Limitations.**

- A separate bug, similar to #58315, remains. The GLM tool grammar allows the special `<tool_call>` token inside `<arg_value>`. When the model quotes tool-result text that contains it, arguments break (`Write({})`, missing arguments). Many responses this PR recovers now hit that bug. It will be reported separately.
- Legacy (non-`ParserEngine`) parsers such as `k2_horizon` keep the old behavior until they move to `ParserEngine`.
- Under spec decode, the target can still reject a draft and then sample an implicit end token that the grammar rejects. This predates the PR. @yzong-rh plans to file an issue for it.
- Also unchanged: a prompt that already ends with an implicit end token (`continue_final_message`) still starts the grammar after it, and multi-token text markers cannot be expressed as a token-id set.

**Related.** No open PR changes where the grammar starts after reasoning; #36138, #56403, #57718 and #57754 touch nearby paths.

This PR was investigated and drafted with an AI assistant (Claude). The tests and live runs listed here were run on real hardware, and a human reviewed the PR before submission.
