commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Forward the reasoning wiring to the engine for batch chat completions
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`/v1/chat/completions/batch` never tells the engine how to treat reasoning:
`create_batch_chat_completion` hard-codes `reasoning_ended=None` and leaves
`reasoning_parser_kwargs` unset, while `/v1/chat/completions` computes both.

Both fields travel on the request into `EngineCoreRequest` and are consumed by
`StructuredOutputManager._get_reasoner()`, which rebuilds the request-local
reasoning parser from the forwarded `chat_template_kwargs` -- its own comment
says it does so precisely "so the structured-output gate observes the same
template kwargs used by the frontend".

Without them a template-kwarg-driven parser silently falls back to its default.
With `--reasoning-parser kimi_k3` (or `deepseek_v3`) and
`chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}` the single-conversation
endpoint builds an engine-side parser with thinking disabled, so
`is_reasoning_end()` answers True on the prompt and the grammar is applied from
the first token. The batch endpoint built the same parser with thinking
*enabled*, `is_reasoning_end()` answered False, and the structured-output gate
never opened: a batch request that asked for `response_format` received
unconstrained output, with no error to show for it.

This is the batch half of the wiring proposed in #42105; the batch endpoint is
still unwired on main.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MoE] Size the permute scratch from its inputs
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Stop predicting the MoE permute scratch capacity from `FusedMoEConfig`; size it from the inputs it actually receives, growing until the workspace manager is locked. This is intended as the root fix behind #55105 (DeepEP v2 + sequence parallelism) and #60423 (PCP), which each patch a different term of the same capacity formula for the `assert n_token <= self.max_num_tokens` failure in the Humming grouped path.

## Claims

- The Humming grouped experts no longer derive a row bound from `max_num_tokens * dp_size * experts_per_token`, so DP, sequence parallelism, PCP, and DeepEP v2's power-of-two receive buckets cannot make the scratch too small.
- The scratch no longer has a hidden-state buffer or dtype, which removes the `hidden_states.dtype == self.hidden_dtype` mismatch on the prequantized (block-FP8 activation) path.
- `CutlassExpertsFp8` and the CUTLASS W4A8 experts get the same behavior. They sized the scratch with `max_num_tokens` and no `dp_size` factor.
- One scratch is shared per `(num_experts, num_local_experts, device)` instead of one per `(capacity, topk, hidden size, dtype)`.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_permute_unpermute.py tests/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py -k "permute or humming or cutlass or block_fp8"` (1x B300) | 906 passed (with `tests/kernels/moe/test_cutlass_moe.py` and `-k "permute or humming or cutlass"`) |
| GSM8K, `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4`, `--moe-backend humming`, `VLLM_HUMMING_MOE_GEMM_TYPE=grouped_contiguous`, 1x B300, eager (existing `configs/humming/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4-humming.yaml`) | 0.8817 on 1319 questions (threshold 0.86), 0 invalid |
| GSM8K, same model, DP=2 + EP, `allgather_reducescatter`, CUDA graphs, `--max-num-batched-tokens 3000` | 0.8969 on 1319 questions (threshold 0.86), 0 invalid |
| `pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py -k "test_reload_weights and FP8_DYNAMIC"` (1x B300, `VLLM_CUTLASS` FP8 backend, in-place weight reload) | 1 passed, 1 skipped; failed in CI before the shared-scratch fix |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with PCP on 8x H20 (SM90), run by @wangyicong52 (results in #59857) | reported working; #60423 closed in favor of this PR |
| pre-commit on changed files, `mypy-3.12` | passed |

Not validated:

- The DeepEP v2 topology from #55105 is not reproduced here: DeepEP v2 is unavailable on the test machine (NCCL 2.29.7 < 2.30.4). @elvircrn, could you try this branch on your setup?
- The prequantized Humming grouped path (block-FP8 activations before dispatch) was not run with real kernels; in-tree coverage of `HummingGroupedExperts.apply` is mock-based. It is guarded by dtype and shape assertions.

## Details

**Root cause.** `workspace13`/`workspace2` are sized from the actual `M` and grow until `lock_workspace()`. `MoEPermuteScratch` was instead sized up front from config, which requires knowing how many rows every prepare/finalize backend can return in every topology. That bound is a property of the dispatcher, not of the experts, and it has been wrong for PCP, for DeepEP v2 with non-power-of-two capacities, and for CUTLASS with DP.

**Change.**

- `MoEPermuteScratch` holds only index metadata and gains `reserve(expanded_rows)`. It reallocates while the workspace manager is unlocked and raises `Scratch growth is not allowed after locking` afterwards, matching the shared workspace's contract.
- Permuted hidden states come from the caller's workspace. CUTLASS already passed a `workspace2` slice. Humming's prequantized path now writes into `quanted_gate_up_input`, which is allocated with the right shape and dtype and is otherwise unused when w13 quantization is skipped, so this costs no extra memory.
- The index buffers stay a persistent resource rather than moving into `get_simultaneous`: a second `get_simultaneous` call inside `apply()` would alias the live `workspace13`/`workspace2`, and `token_expert_indices` is an `arange` that would otherwise be refilled every call. They are small (seven int32 arrays over the expanded rows plus the sort workspace).

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**

- A runtime shape larger than anything seen during warmup still fails, with the same contract and at the same point as `workspace13`.
- `moe_permute(scratch=...)` without `permuted_hidden_states` now allocates that tensor per call. Both in-tree callers pass a buffer; `benchmark_moe_permute_unpermute.py`'s scratch numbers are not comparable to earlier ones.
- `get_persistent_resource`'s docstring is loosened from "must not resize" to "must not resize once the manager is locked".
- The CUTLASS experts use the same shared scratch as Humming. A scratch owned by the experts instance broke weight reload: the experts are rebuilt after the workspace is locked, so the new scratch was empty and could not grow (caught by `test_reload_weights` in CI build 93385).
- Anything that first reaches a scratch-using path after the lock, without that path having run during warmup, now fails where the old fixed-size scratch would have allocated lazily.

**Relation to open PRs.** Not a duplicate: #55105 and #60423 extend the capacity formula for one topology each and conflict with each other; this removes the formula. The DeepEP v2 handle-capacity change in #55105 (`next_power_of_2(ceil(max_num_tokens / sp_size))`) is independent and still useful. Searches for `MoEPermuteScratch` and `permute scratch workspace` found no other open PR.

commits.pr_title: [Attention] Allow an NVFP4 KV cache on SM90 with fa2
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

[#46963](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46963) reads an NVFP4 KV cache through FlashInfer's fa2 path on SM8x and SM12x. SM90 is left out although it is in the same position: it has no FP4 conversion instructions, so FlashInfer dequantizes NVFP4 there in software as on SM8x (its prefill notes that every pre-SM100 target runs the same generic 1-byte-KV fa2 path), and FlashInfer's FA3 backend rejects an NVFP4 KV cache. This adds SM90 to the architectures that read NVFP4 with fa2.

## Claims

- `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4` is accepted with FlashInfer on SM90 and takes the writer and fa2 prefill and decode paths that SM8x uses.
- SM90 decode stays on fa2: the existing NVFP4 exclusion keeps it off XQA, whose NVFP4 path FlashInfer limits to SM12x. NVFP4 on SM90 reports single-token decode CUDA graph support, so with speculative decoding the graph mode drops from FULL to PIECEWISE or NONE, depending on the compilation config.
- Nothing changes on other architectures.

## Validation

Not run on SM90: there is no SM90 hardware here. The SM90 path is checked against FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1's source:

- `vec_dtypes.cuh` uses the `cvt ... e2m1x2` instructions only for `__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 1000`; SM8x and SM90 take the same software conversion.
- `is_fa3_backend_supported` returns `False` for a `uint8` (NVFP4) KV cache, so the `"auto"` prefill and decode wrappers vLLM creates resolve to fa2 on SM90.
- `xqa.py` asserts that XQA reads NVFP4 only on SM12x, and vLLM keeps an NVFP4 cache off XQA through `nvfp4_fa2`.

`test_flashinfer_nvfp4_kv_cache_update`, which checks the writer and the data/scale views against FlashInfer's NVFP4 dequantization, now also runs on SM90. On SM80, where nothing changes, `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer.py -k nvfp4` gives 4 passed and `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_dcp_spec_reorder.py -k flashinfer` gives 29 passed, 5 skipped, the same as on `main`; with `tests/kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py` added and `-k "flashinfer or nvfp4"`, 39 passed, 9 skipped.

## Details

`_nvfp4_kv_on_fa2` now includes SM90, so `supports_kv_cache_dtype` accepts `nvfp4` there, the builder and the impl set `nvfp4_fa2`, and queries stay in the model dtype. `supports_combination` also includes SM90, so head size 64 and attention sinks are refused up front as on SM8x and SM12x, and DCP is refused in the builder as there.

FlashInfer turns off split-KV for NVFP4 only on SM12x, where corruption was reported. Its source records an SM90 check (head_dim 128, the asymmetric 512/256 path and a needle swept across split boundaries) in which split-KV on and off agreed to output rounding, so SM90 keeps split-KV as SM8x does. This vLLM integration has not run on SM90.

[#60452](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60452) removes the NVFP4 exclusion from XQA selection so SM12x can decode NVFP4 with XQA. If both land, SM90 has to stay off XQA for NVFP4, so whichever lands second limits both decode selection and `get_cudagraph_support` to SM12x for NVFP4; blocking it only in `forward` would leave the graph support wrong.

On SM90 an FP8 cache uses FA3 prefill and XQA decode while NVFP4 uses fa2 for both; the throughput difference is not measured here.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Close MessageQueue zmq resources via finalizer to avoid exit
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes an intermittent hang where a spawned EngineCore never exits after a startup failure, timing out `tests/v1/shutdown/test_startup_error.py::test_async_llm_startup_error[forward-2-...]` (seen on AMD CI in `Distributed Torchrun + Shutdown`, which runs with `spawn`). Related: #60121, #60141.

### Root cause

Each `MessageQueue` owns a private zmq `Context` and sockets that are never closed explicitly. After a failed `collective_rpc`, the executor's response `MessageQueue` is only reachable through a reference cycle (`FutureWrapper` → exception → traceback → `collective_rpc` / `get_response` frames → `response_mqs`), so it is freed by the cyclic GC.

When the context and its sockets are collected in the same GC pass, CPython clears the context's weak socket references first. pyzmq's `Context.__del__` → `destroy()` then closes nothing, and `term()` blocks forever on the still-open sockets. pyzmq only skips this after its own atexit hook runs, so the hang occurs when GC triggers inside an earlier atexit hook (e.g. `ray.shutdown`, which lazily imports `ray.dag`).

Evidence:
- Captured stacks of real hangs: `term` ← `destroy` ← `Context.__del__` during GC inside `ray.shutdown`.
- Tracing every engine-process zmq context over 46 runs: the response queue's context (`create_from_handle`) was freed by cyclic GC in exactly the 2 runs that hung, and was not freed or was freed by refcount in the 44 that passed.
- A minimal pure-pyzmq repro (context and socket in a cycle, `gc.collect()`) hangs every time, even with `LINGER=0`, and does not hang without the cycle.

## Fix

Register a `weakref.finalize` per `MessageQueue` that holds the context and sockets, closes the sockets with `linger=0`, then terminates the context.
- The context can no longer be collected as garbage, so the deadlocking `Context.__del__` path is unreachable.
- The finalizer only runs once the queue is unreachable, so no other thread can be using its sockets.
- `atexit = False` keeps exit-time behavior unchanged for queues still alive at shutdown.

## Test Plan

- New `test_reader_in_reference_cycle_is_collected_without_blocking` in `tests/distributed/test_shm_broadcast.py`.
- `pytest tests/distributed/test_shm_broadcast.py`
- Loop the startup-error test with `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn` on MI300X.

## Test Result

- New test fails on main (GC blocks) and passes with this change; full `test_shm_broadcast.py`: 31 passed.
- Startup-error test with spawn on MI300X (TP=2, CPU limited to match CI): **10 hangs in 544 runs before → 0 hangs in 298 runs after** (expected about 5.5 at the baseline rate).
- pre-commit passes.

## Summary

`incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` is the block-diffusion (DFlash2) drafter published for `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`. On current `main` the pair cannot be served: `vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2",...}'` fails during startup, and fixing one failure exposes the next. This PR makes the combination start and serve on NVIDIA (8x H100, TP8 + EP), adds unit coverage for the two non-model changes, and reports a throughput sweep against the existing MTP path. No kernels, defaults, or MTP behaviour are changed.

The three blockers on `main` (9d4d9aa5bc), in the order they surface:

| # | Stage | Error on `main` | Root cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | draft model load | `RuntimeError: Model does not support EAGLE3 interface` | `Glm5NextForCausalLM` / `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` (the architecture the DFlash2 checkpoint targets) do not declare `SupportsEagle3`, and `Glm5NextModel` is not an `EagleModelMixin`, so the DFlash speculator cannot register its aux hidden-state layers (`target_layer_ids + 1 = [6, 15, 25, 34, 43]`). |
| 2 | KV cache init | `NotImplementedError: Layer language_model.model.layers.3.self_attn.indexer.k_cache: page size is not divisible by the maximum page size and cannot be padded. Padding is only supported for non-MLA attention layers.` | `_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next` bails out as soon as a non-MLA attention layer (the draft's sliding-window GQA layers) is present, so the generic page unifier runs on a spec set it cannot unify (MLA 655,360 B, indexer 21,120 B and draft 163,840 B pages at block_size 640). |
| 3 | config | `ValueError: Number of experts in the model must be greater than 0 when expert parallelism is enabled` | `create_draft_parallel_config` copies `enable_expert_parallel` from the MoE target onto the dense drafter (introduced by #55914 for the DeepSeek-V4 MegaMoE drafter). |

### Changes

- **`vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/model.py` (aux hidden-state capture).** `Glm5NextModel` becomes an `EagleModelMixin`; `Glm5NextForCausalLM` and `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` declare `SupportsEagle3`. The tensor handed to the drafter is not `hidden_states + residual`: GLM-5.3-Flash layers run mHC with 4 residual streams and defer each layer's `hc_post` into the next layer's fused post+pre kernel, so at a layer boundary `residual` is the widened `(T, 4 * hidden)` stream (a naive `hidden + residual` fails with `The size of tensor a (8192) must match the size of tensor b (4) at non-singleton dimension 1`) and `hidden_states` alone is the raw layer output. `_aux_hidden_state()` completes the deferred `hc_post` through a dedicated `MHCPostOp` and contracts the streams back to `hidden_size` with `hc_contract`, which is the quantity SGLang's `_prepare_aux_hidden_state` feeds DFlash2. The capture is read-only: the layer loop keeps consuming the original `(hidden_states, residual, post, comb)` tuple. Non-mHC layer boundaries already carry the summed stream in `hidden_states` and are returned as-is. When any aux layer is requested, `forward` returns `(hidden_states, aux_hidden_states)`; otherwise the return type is unchanged.

### Relationship to existing PRs (duplicate check run on 2026-09-15)

Searches: `gh pr list --state open --search "dflash glm"`, `"GLM-5.3 speculative draft"`, `"create_draft_parallel_config"`, `"enable_expert_parallel draft model"`, `gh pr list --state all --search "dflash"`, `gh issue list --search "GLM-5.3-Flash dflash"`.

- #55682 (Leoyzen, open) implements the aux capture with the same semantics (materialize `hc_post`, then `hc_contract`, at the layer boundary) and adds a CPU unit suite for it. It intentionally leaves the KV-cache layout to a companion change (its description notes the draft sliding-window groups still need one); on the configuration tested here (TP8, `--kv-cache-dtype auto`, H100) `main` + an aux-capture-only change still fails at blocker 2. The `model.py` change here is functionally equivalent for GLM-5.3-Flash's mHC boundaries; if #55682 lands first, this PR rebases onto it and drops its `model.py` hunk.
- #55423 (zixi-qi, draft, needs-rebase) covers aux capture plus a KV layout, but with a different layout design: the draft's sliding-window layers are re-blocked to the MLA block size, padded to the MLA page and aliased into the target's MLA slots (no extra bytes per block; `is_eagle_group` follows `use_eagle_block_drop()`; tested with `disable_eagle_block_drop=true`). This PR keeps the draft in a separate region with its native page instead; it is simpler and needs no block-drop override, but it costs KV capacity (numbers below). The two are alternative designs for reviewers to choose between.
- #56933 (hnt2601, opened 2026-09-15) is the same EP-inheritance fix with a different signature (`draft_model_config: ModelConfig | None`). If it merges first, this PR drops the `speculative.py` hunk.
- #55219 (ivanium, draft) removes the GLM-specific layout in favour of the generic packed layout; if that lands, the `kv_cache_utils.py` part of this PR is superseded.
- #54451 (ROCm: glm5next lacks `SupportsEagle3`) is the ROCm counterpart of blocker 1; this PR only touches the NVIDIA model file.

No open PR makes `GLM-5.3-Flash + GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` start on `main` end to end; this one does, and the parts overlapping with #55682 and #56933 are flagged above for rebasing.

Due to discussion for kv cache allocation,  this PR just submits the main support in advance.

## Previous full supported performance

**Setup.** 8x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (driver 535.154.05), TP8 + EP, torch 2.13.0+cu129, FlashInfer 0.6.18, Python 3.12, vLLM `main` 9d4d9aa5bc + this branch, V2 model runner (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`). Target `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (fp8 weights, `--kv-cache-dtype auto`, `--max-model-len 131072`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9`, `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune`, `--tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 --enable-auto-tool-choice`). Draft `incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` (5 sliding-window layers, sliding window 2048, block_size 8). Auto-selected attention backends: FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90 (target), FLASH_ATTN (draft).

**Workload.** 16 fixed prompts (code and prose), greedy (`temperature=0`), `max_tokens=512`, `/v1/chat/completions`. Single stream = 4 sequential prompts after 2 warm-ups; concurrency N = N simultaneous requests (prompts cycled). Aggregate output tok/s, per-request median tok/s in parentheses. `k` = `num_speculative_tokens`, "FA" / "FI" = FlashAttention / FlashInfer draft attention, the number in the config column is `--max-num-seqs`.

| Config | Single stream | Conc 8 | Conc 32 | Conc 64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DFlash2 k=16, FA, 48 | 178.7 | 848.5 (118.3) | 707.3 (23.1) | - |
| DFlash2 k=8, FA, 48 | 202.1 | 987.7 (136.3) | 2652.5 (94.5) | - |
| DFlash2 k=6, FA, 48 | 218.5 | 1064.5 (145.2) | 2844.3 (101.2) | - |
| DFlash2 k=4, FA, 48 | 220.3 | 1051.3 (148.0) | 2751.6 (98.8) | - |
| DFlash2 k=6, FI, 48 | 202.1 | 1021.0 (141.1) | 2578.8 (95.1) | - |
| **DFlash2 k=6, FA, 96** (run 1) | **223.0** | **1074.0 (145.2)** | **2850.7 (103.9)** | - |
| **DFlash2 k=6, FA, 96** (run 2) | **225.5** | - | **2923.6 (106.7)** | **4269.3 (77.5)** |
| MTP k=5, 96 (baseline) | 160.7 | 853.7 (117.3) | 2377.0 (84.0) | 3721.3 (66.7) |

Acceptance, aggregated from every `SpecDecoding metrics` log line of each run:

| Config | Mean acceptance length | Draft acceptance rate | Per-position acceptance |
|---|---|---|---|
| DFlash2 k=16 | 3.63 | 16.5% | 0.75, 0.54, 0.39, 0.28, 0.20, 0.14, 0.10, 0.08, 0.05, 0.04, 0.02, 0.01, 0.006, 0.004, 0.002, 0.001 |
| DFlash2 k=8 | 3.33 | 29.1% | 0.75, 0.53, 0.36, 0.25, 0.18, 0.12, 0.08, 0.06 |
| DFlash2 k=6 | 3.31 | 38.5% | 0.77, 0.55, 0.39, 0.28, 0.19, 0.13 |
| DFlash2 k=4 | 3.00 | 49.9% | 0.78, 0.56, 0.39, 0.27 |
| MTP k=5 | 3.13 | 42.7% | 0.81, 0.57, 0.37, 0.23, 0.15 |

Takeaways:

- `num_speculative_tokens` is the dominant knob. Acceptance decays to ~0 beyond position 8 (the drafter's block_size), so k=16 pays a 17-token verify per step for the same ~3.3-3.6 accepted tokens; going to k=6 raises conc-32 throughput from 707 to 2924 tok/s (4.1x). k=4..6 is the sweet spot on this workload, k=8 is slightly worse.
- Against MTP k=5 at identical settings, DFlash2 k=6 is faster at every concurrency: +40% single stream, +26% at 8, +23% at 32, +15% at 64.
- FlashInfer as the draft attention backend is 7-9% slower than the auto-selected FlashAttention.
- `--max-num-seqs 96` vs 48: +2-3%, no preemption at concurrency 64.

**KV cache capacity (cost of the separate draft region).**

| Config | Available KV memory | KV capacity | Max concurrency at 131072 tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| MTP k=5 | 23.61 GiB | 1,802,673 tokens | 13.75x |
| DFlash2 k=6 | 23.49 GiB | 1,358,649 tokens | 10.37x |

Per block (block_size 640) the target uses 11 x 655,360 B MLA pages plus 11 x 21,120 B indexer pages (kpool tails aliased into them); the draft adds 5 x 163,840 B pages and its own per-request block demand to the group-aware capacity estimate, hence 24.6% fewer tokens than MTP at the same memory. #55423's slot-aliasing design avoids this at the price of re-blocking the draft to the MLA page; that is the main trade-off between the two PRs. At `--max-num-seqs 96` this still leaves ~14k tokens per sequence.

## Test Plan

```bash
# Unit tests
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_get_kv_cache_config_glm5_with_dflash_draft_group "tests/test_config.py::test_draft_parallel_config_inherits_ep_only_for_moe_drafters" -v

# Lint and types
pre-commit run --files vllm/config/speculative.py vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/model.py vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py tests/test_config.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py

# Serve (8x H100)
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --served-model-name glm-5.3-flash --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --kv-cache-dtype auto --max-num-seqs 96 --max-model-len 131072 --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":6}'
# MTP baseline: same command with --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}'

# Tool-calling E2E: 8 scenarios against /v1/chat/completions (auto / required / named tool_choice, zero-arg tool, no tools, thinking off, streaming, multi-turn), see Test Result
# Throughput sweep: 16 prompts, greedy, max_tokens=512, single stream + concurrency {8,32} / {32,64}; per-config server relaunch with the speculative-config JSON above
# Accuracy
.venv/bin/python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 1
```

## Test Result

**Unit tests.** `3 passed` (the kv-cache test and both parametrizations of the config test).

**pre-commit.** All hooks pass on the five changed files, including `mypy-3.10` (the follow-up commit fixes a `dict` invariance error in `_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next`).

**Startup.** Each blocker above was hit and cleared in turn on this branch; the final configuration loads the draft (5 layers, `Overriding draft model max model len from 1048576 to 131072`), builds the KV cache (`GPU KV cache size: 1,358,649 tokens`), captures CUDA graphs and serves.

**Tool-calling E2E** against the running DFlash2 server (`--tool-call-parser glm47`, `--reasoning-parser glm45`): 8/8 pass, zero FSM or CUDA errors in the server log. Repeated after each sweep configuration with the same result.

| Scenario | Checks | Result |
|---|---|---|
| auto tool call | `tool_choice=auto`, one `<tool_call>` parsed into `tool_calls`, arguments valid JSON | PASS |
| required tool call | `tool_choice=required` forces a call | PASS |
| named tool call | `tool_choice={"type":"function","function":{"name":...}}` picks the named tool | PASS |
| named zero-argument tool | tool without parameters yields `arguments == "{}"` | PASS |
| no tools, plain chat | no tool schema, ordinary completion, no stray tags | PASS |
| thinking off | `chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}` with tools | PASS |
| streaming tool call | `stream=true`, deltas reassemble to a valid call | PASS |
| multi-turn | tool result fed back, second assistant turn answers from it | PASS |

**GSM8K (5-shot, 1319 questions, greedy, `max_tokens=256`, `--max-concurrency 1 --request-timeout-seconds 7200`; the default 600 s timeout acts as a global deadline at concurrency 1 and truncates the run).**

| Server | Accuracy | Invalid responses | Output tokens | Wall time | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Target only (no speculative config), same machine and flags | 0.931 | 0.0% | 121,390 | 1195 s | 101.6 |
| DFlash2 k=6 (this PR) | 0.939 | 0.0% | 123,732 | 607 s | 203.8 |

The two accuracies differ by 0.8 points (about 10 of 1319 questions), inside the run-to-run spread of this greedy-but-nondeterministic stack (see below); output-token counts match within 2%. DFlash2 delivers the same accuracy at 2.0x the single-stream decode speed.

**Greedy output determinism.** Exact token-level lossless verification is not possible on this stack: with `temperature=0` the same server produces different continuations run to run (16 sweep prompts, 512 tokens, sequential, prompt already cached): target-only 0/16 identical across three runs (median common prefix 272-306 characters before the first divergence), DFlash2 k=6 0/16 identical across three runs (median 237-306), and DFlash2 vs target-only 0/16 identical (median 222-237). The run-to-run spread of the target alone is the same size as the DFlash2-vs-target spread, so the divergence comes from the fp8 MoE + EP numerics of the target (near-tie argmax flips), not from the speculative path; the GSM8K parity above (0.919 vs 0.911) is the meaningful losslessness check.

**Pre-existing crash observed while testing, not introduced by this PR (#55626).** Any step that co-schedules a ~600+ token prefill with a speculative verify step, or a burst of a dozen ~630-token prefills, kills the engine with an asynchronous CUDA fault. It reproduces identically with MTP, whose KV layout on this branch is byte-for-byte the `main` layout, so it is a property of the target's FlashInfer SM90 sparse-MLA path with speculative decoding, matching the traceback location and the FlashInfer core dump posted in #55626.

| Run | Speculative config | Load | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | DFlash2 k=6 | `gsm8k_eval.py` unbounded (100 in flight): 12 prefills of 618-645 tokens in one step, 7578 tokens | `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`, all 8 workers, reproduced 3/3 |
| A' | DFlash2 k=6, `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` | same | fault attributed to FlashInfer `BatchMLAPagedAttentionSM90` in the target's `flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py::forward_mqa` (`Failed to run MLA, error: an illegal memory access was encountered`) |
| B | DFlash2 k=6 | `--max-concurrency 2`: one 661-token prefill + one 7-token verify step | `CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED` (sticky error surfacing in the next GEMM) |
| C | MTP k=5 (main layout) | unbounded: 7 prefills, 4518 tokens | `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` |
| D | MTP k=5 (main layout) | `--max-concurrency 2`: one 637-token prefill + one 6-token verify step | `CUDA error: an illegal instruction was encountered`, surfacing at `flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py:350 _kv_lens_host` (the same frame as in #55626) |

The throughput sweep and the tool-calling E2E never hit it because their concurrent prompts are short (~30 tokens) and their long prompts run one at a time; GSM8K was therefore run at `--max-concurrency 1`. Prefix caching is not involved (`prefix_cache_stats ... hits=0` in every crash dump).

## Known limitations / follow-ups

- #55626 (above) affects every speculative configuration of GLM-5.3-Flash on SM90 and needs a separate fix; the DFlash2 path inherits it.
- The separate draft region costs KV capacity relative to the slot-aliasing design in #55423 (24.6% fewer tokens than MTP at the same memory); the two designs should be reconciled in review.
- Aux hidden states are not all-gathered under sequence parallelism (`compilation_config.pass_config.enable_sp`); the tested configuration runs with compilation mode NONE, where SP is off. Pipeline parallelism is already gated off for GLM-5.3-Flash and was not exercised.
- Tested with greedy sampling for throughput and the default sampling of the tool-calling scripts; `disable_eagle_block_drop` was left at its default.
- Only the NVIDIA model file is changed; the ROCm copy (#54451) is not addressed.

commits.pr_title: [MoE] MXFP4 oracle: add CUTLASS W4A4 backend and BF16 activation fallback
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

First step of #54959 for the packed MXFP4 MoE methods. This PR only touches the MXFP4 oracle; no quant method changes behaviour yet.

**Contract.** The `activation_key` passed to `select_mxfp4_moe_backend` is the activation precision the checkpoint declares (`None` = BF16). Backends that match it are preferred. If none supports the deployment, the oracle falls back to BF16-activation backends and logs a warning, so a W4A4 checkpoint runs as W4A16 on hardware without a W4A4 kernel. Activations are never quantized below what the checkpoint declares.

Previously a non-`None` key was an exact filter, so a W4A4 checkpoint raised on any deployment without a W4A4 kernel (including `--moe-backend marlin`). This matches the MXFP4 linear kernels, where weight-only kernels already accept MXFP4 activation keys as a fallback.

**CUTLASS W4A4 backend.** `CUTLASS_MXFP4_MXFP4` (vLLM's `CutlassExpertsMxfp4`) is added to the oracle: enum, kernel class, scale swizzle in `convert_weight_to_mxfp4_moe_kernel_format`, quant config and 128 round-up. Today that kernel is only reachable through device probes hand-rolled in `CompressedTensorsW4A4Mxfp4MoEMethod` and `INCMxfp4MoEMethod`.

**Behaviour change for existing callers.** Callers that pass no activation key (gpt-oss) and callers of `select_deepseek_v4_mxfp4_moe_backend` (DeepSeek-V4, Kimi-K3) select the same backend as main for every `--moe-backend` value I compared. Callers that already pass a key (online MXFP4, Quark W4A4 and static-FP8 W4A8) change only where main raises:

| Caller | `--moe-backend` | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Online MXFP4 / Quark W4A4 | auto | raises | CUTLASS W4A4 |
| Online MXFP4 / Quark W4A4 | marlin, flashinfer_trtllm, triton_unfused, humming | raises | that backend, BF16 activations |
| Quark W4A8 static FP8 | auto | raises | TRTLLM BF16 |
| Quark W4A8 static FP8 | marlin, flashinfer_trtllm, triton_unfused, humming | raises | that backend, BF16 activations |
| gpt-oss with `quantization_config.moe.activation=mxfp8` | marlin, triton, triton_unfused, humming | raises | that backend, BF16 activations |

Measured on NVIDIA SM103 without `amd-quark`. I have not loaded a model through these newly reachable combinations, and could not measure ROCm. With `amd-quark` installed on CUDA SM100, W4A4 would select CUTLASS ahead of EMULATION.

**Relation to #59460.** The fallback is the default here; #59460 (`VLLM_STRICT_QUANT_SCHEME`) is the opt-in to refuse it. This PR passes BF16 fallback backends their own key, so whichever lands second should pass the checkpoint key through and let `executed_activation_key` report the downgrade, replacing the warning added here.

**Why this is split out.** #55232, #56306 and #56523 each move the CUTLASS swizzle into the oracle and each add a different selection path next to it (an `input_quant` flag, `select_w4a4_mxfp4_moe_backend`, a `candidates=` list). The mechanical part is the same in all three; the selection contract is what differs and what review has stalled on. This PR settles the contract in the existing `activation_key` argument, with no new entrypoint. A follow-up reduces the compressed-tensors and INC methods to weight creation plus oracle delegation.

Not a duplicate: those PRs change the quant methods; this one does not, and is intended as the base they (or the follow-up) build on.

**Follow-up motivation (measured on main, NVIDIA B300).** `CompressedTensorsW4A4Mxfp4MoEMethod` selects `CutlassExpertsMxfp4` with MXFP4 activations for every checkpoint and every `--moe-backend` except `b12x`, including weight-only (A16) checkpoints, and fails on shapes that are not 128-aligned (`shape '[960, 34]' is invalid for input of size 36864`).

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py -k select_mxfp4
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_cutlass_moe.py -k oracle_matches
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py tests/kernels/moe/test_cutlass_moe.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_b12x.py tests/kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py \
  tests/quantization/test_gfx950_moe.py tests/quantization/test_online.py \
  tests/quantization/test_quark.py tests/quantization/test_auto_round.py \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp4_kernel_selection.py
pre-commit run; pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual
```

- `test_select_mxfp4_moe_backend_respects_checkpoint_activation` (CPU): exact match wins, BF16 fallback (auto and explicit backend), BF16 checkpoint never quantized.
- `test_cutlass_mxfp4_oracle_matches_direct_kernel` (SM100): the oracle-built kernel equals calling `run_cutlass_moe_mxfp4` with manually swizzled scales.

To check the API is sufficient, I also prototyped the follow-up (compressed-tensors method as a thin `Mxfp4MoEMethod` subclass that passes the checkpoint activation to this oracle) and compared it with main through a real `RoutedExperts` layer on a B300.

## Test Result

NVIDIA B300 (SM103): 2552 passed, 77 skipped, 5 failed across the suites above. The same 5 fail on unmodified main on this machine and are unrelated (Int8 unsupported on SM103, a DeepGEMM JIT panic, MXFP8 AutoRound). pre-commit and mypy pass.

Three of the four new selection cases fail on main and pass here.

Follow-up prototype vs main (layer harness, random MXFP4 weights, B300):

| Checkpoint / backend | main | prototype on this oracle |
|---|---|---|
| W4A4, auto | CUTLASS W4A4 | CUTLASS W4A4, bitwise equal to main |
| W4A4, auto, Renormalize routing | CUTLASS W4A4 | CUTLASS W4A4, bitwise equal to main |
| W4A4, `--moe-backend marlin` | CUTLASS W4A4 (flag ignored) | Marlin W4A16 |
| W4A4, hidden 1088 / intermediate 480 | reshape error | CUTLASS W4A4, padded to 1152 / 512 |
| W4A16, auto | CUTLASS W4A4 | TRTLLM BF16 |
| W4 + dynamic FP8 (group 128), auto | CUTLASS W4A4 | TRTLLM BF16 (fallback, warned) |

ROCm, XPU and CPU paths were not run; the ROCm selection tests are skipped on this machine. No model evals were run, since no quant method changes in this PR.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write and validate this change.

## Overview

Guard MiniMax-M3's Triton sparse-decode block-table dereference against negative sentinel and out-of-range logical block indices. The independent metadata-producer correction remains #54604.

Rebased on October 5, 2026 onto public main `54d93af9fb89d0bb8392bdb72db42bb6a17cb4ca`; head `4a4e4ee62ddc232d930a2666403356cad436eefc`. All four PR patches are unchanged according to `git range-diff`. Main still has the unguarded dereference. Ready for code review, with the remaining validation below explicit.

## Claims

- Invalid top-k entries cannot become block-table or KV-cache pointers.
- Invalid entries leave the online-softmax state unchanged; the loop stays branch-free.
- A standalone B200 CI job runs the existing complete MiniMax-M3 attention suite so failures in unrelated, earlier commands cannot suppress it. Existing reference-accuracy thresholds are unchanged.

## Validation

- October 5: `pre-commit run --from-ref 54d93af9fb89d0bb8392bdb72db42bb6a17cb4ca --to-ref HEAD` and `git diff --check` passed.
- The guard and its 16-case regression are unchanged by this rebase; main's surrounding test updates are retained.
- On the previous head `1e2fc48cc515`, [Buildkite #92185's standalone B200 job](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/92185#01a0f2f9-6c4f-4d2d-85f8-6333e30423ef) passed: **121 passed, 45 skipped**. The overall build failed in the [AMD sleep-mode job](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/92185#01a0f2f9-6bac-422d-8e98-e27571c39844), which exited with code 139; the full build is not claimed as green.
- Earlier head `dafeddcc063f` passed all 16 regression cases on each of B200, L4, and MI300 (**48 total**) in [Buildkite #91309](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91309). Historical results validate those exact commits, not the October 5 head.
- A fresh `/ci run` started [Buildkite #92915](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/92915) for the October 5 head `4a4e4ee62ddc232d930a2666403356cad436eefc`. Current-head GPU results are pending.
- No GPU tests ran locally during this refresh: the local environment has no CUDA/ROCm device. End-to-end serving reproduction, unfixed-kernel negative controls, and all-valid decode-latency measurements remain outstanding. No performance or model-quality result is claimed.

Reproduce the focused suite on a supported accelerator:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py \
  -k 'decode_sparse_attention or decode_wrong_layout' -v
```

## Details

Triton's `bt_row + blk` uses raw pointer arithmetic. For `blk == -1`, the unsafe access reads immediately before the request's row, not its final element. The regression uses contiguous rows and runs request 1 with a poisoned final entry in row 0, making this address deterministic.

The kernel maps invalid logical blocks to safe block 0, masks their K/V and scale loads, and preserves softmax state for those entries. The upper bound is this query token's `ceil(kv_len / 128)`: a block that becomes valid for a later speculative token contributes nothing to the earlier token because it was already fully causally masked. This does not redefine all-empty query output in the merge kernel.

The regression covers negative and large positive invalid indices, invalid-before/after-valid orderings, split-K and single-chunk execution, both KV layouts, eager execution, capture, and three graph replays. It requires finite output and exact parity with a valid-only run on identical inputs; independent FP32-reference tests and their tolerances are unchanged. Run unfixed-kernel controls in a dedicated process because an illegal access can poison the device context.

Open-PR searches were refreshed on October 5. Related #56932 adds specialized decode paths but does not replace the general-loop guard; #57420 concerns prefill, #49054 empty-row merge NaNs, and #52060 scalar KV scales. This PR does not duplicate those changes.

The checklist review found no new rebase-related code issue. The scope remains a local kernel safety fix plus regression/CI coverage; it adds no model-runner or scheduler policy.

commits.pr_title: [Doc] Require GCC 13 for CUDA source builds
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Updates vLLM's CUDA source-build compiler requirement from GCC ≥ 11.3 to GCC ≥ 13, in the installation documentation and via an early CMake check.

Fixes #58158

## Claims

- The CUDA installation guide states the GCC 13 floor and notes that Ubuntu 24.04 (the base of the default vLLM image) ships GCC 13 by default.
- CMake fails configure early with a clear message when building for CUDA with GCC < 13, instead of failing later inside dependency host compilation with `fatal error: format: No such file or directory`.
- CPU builds are unaffected; their recommended toolchain remains gcc/g++ ≥ 12.3, and the existing top-level GCC ≥ 11.3 PyTorch C++20 check is unchanged.

## Validation

- DeepSelect pin `d96d33a` includes `<format>` in host code: [csrc/api.cpp](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepSelect/blob/d96d33afe1fab0d6066da49cdc91e64c2bee65ea/csrc/api.cpp#L17)
- DeepGEMM pin `1e1842a8` unconditionally includes `<format>` in the host include chain: [csrc/apis/attention.hpp](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/blob/1e1842a833699298f7afc02eefb2ed168fff6938/csrc/apis/attention.hpp#L4)
- GCC 11.4 reproduction of the failure: the v0.30.0 wheel build fails with `fatal error: format: No such file or directory` when the DeepSelect/DeepGEMM host targets compile (evidence recorded in #58158)
- The new CMake check is scoped to `VLLM_GPU_LANG STREQUAL "CUDA"`, matching the gate that includes DeepGEMM/DeepSelect (`CMakeLists.txt`, external-projects block)
- `markdownlint-cli2` and `typos` pre-commit hooks pass on the changed files

## Details

Issue #58158 documents that the declared GCC ≥ 11.3 floor drifted from reality: pinned dependencies require C++20 `<format>`, so the effective libstdc++ floor for CUDA source builds is GCC 13. Rather than restoring GCC 11.3 compatibility dependency-by-dependency, this PR documents GCC 13 as the requirement.

The existing top-level GCC ≥ 11.3 check (PyTorch C++20 headers) is still true for all builds and is left unchanged; the new check is additive and CUDA-scoped, so CPU and other device builds see no change.

commits.pr_title: [CI][ROCm] Reuse AITER's prebuilt MoE module in the modular-kernel harness
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`(MI300) MoE Kernels Shard` spends most of its wall time JIT-compiling AITER MoE kernels that the image already ships. In the last internal run the job was killed at the 55 min timeout with **no test failure** 83% of its 3356 s was five AITER builds costing 488–821 s each: [AMD CI #14276](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/14276/list?jid=01a11abf-7405-4180-8176-45e07f6cc5a1&tab=output)

## Why it happens

AITER encodes `preshuffle_on` / `preshuffle_off` in its `moe_ck2stages` module names, but only applies the `--preshuffle` codegen flag for `fp4x2` (`aiter/ops/moe_op.py`). For `bf16`, `f8` and `i8` the two variants are byte-identical source, and only the `on` half is prebuilt.

Production never hits this because `process_weights_after_loading` shuffles the weights. This harness builds its tensors directly, so every `AiterExperts` config asks for a `preshuffle_off` module that is a guaranteed cache miss — on a kernel the image already has under the other name.

## What this PR does

Pre-shuffle the rank weights in `_maybe_convert_weights_for_experts`, next to the existing TrtLLM/FlashInfer conversions, so AITER selects the prebuilt module.

The guard is conditional on the quant scheme, not on shape. The prebuilt `f8_f8` modules are built with `GPU_ARCHS="gfx942;gfx950"` and end up carrying the **gfx950 instance table on a gfx942 host**, so they reject `inter_dim=384` — but only for the fp8 per-tensor and per-token schemes. The JIT rebuild has been accidentally masking that. Unquantized and fp8 block-128 pass at every shape, so they take the prebuilt module; the rest keep compiling until [ROCm/aiter#5766](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/5766) is fixed.

A shape-based guard would not work: module names do not encode `N`, so the same module is shared between a safe shape and an unsafe one in the same shard.

## Measured on MI300

Across the five shards of `test_modular_kernel_combinations.py`, **JIT compiles drop from 19 to 9 (-53%)**.

Every removed compile is `b16_b16` or `f8_f8 per_1x128`; everything left is fp8 per-tensor or per-token, exactly what the guard intentionally leaves on the JIT path. Zero `does not support this GEMM problem` across all five shards, and test counts per shard are unchanged (11 / 19 / 14 / 8).

### Confirmed on a full CI run of this branch

Wall time across the five shards now spans **12–47 min**, where it previously spanned **34 min up
to the 55 min timeout** — the slowest shard never finished. Group latency is set by the slowest
shard, so it goes from a timing-out job to **47 min**, with every shard passing. Per shard:
41→32, 52→36, 40→32, 34→12, and timeout→47.
CI log: https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/14289/list?jid=01a11bb7-d163-46d5-8b05-9e8c377b4cdd&tab=output
## Scope

Test-harness only. The branch is dead code off ROCm (`AiterExperts` is `None` when AITER is absent), and on ROCm it is only reached from `test_modular_kernel_combinations.py`. The reference implementation still receives the original unshuffled weights, so the accuracy comparison is unchanged.

## Still needed, not in this PR

- **[ROCm/aiter#5766](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/5766)** — until the arch guard is fixed,
  the fp8 per-tensor and per-token schemes cannot use the prebuilt modules at all.

commits.pr_title: [Quantization] Enable shared expert fusion compatibility with online `shared_expert` quantization (showcase: along Quark MXFP4 routed experts)
commits.pr_body:
## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

## Purpose

This PR enables compatibility of online `shared_expert` quantization with fused shared expert optimization. As an example, it implements it for for `QuarkOCP_MX_MoEMethod` (and `INCMxfp4MoEMethod` to showcase extensibility, possibly to be removed).

The main idea is that given https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f27ae25473af7520dde3f8b9e0705041940be0c9/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_next.py#L168-L180 `self.shared_expert = Qwen3NextMLP` is not defined when using `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`, we use weight loading in the `RoutedExperts` to capture the shared expert weight loading, quantize it there, and copy the quantized shared expert into the correct quantized fused expert slot.

The original `quant_method` is preserved (e.g. `QuarkOCP_MX_MoEMethod`).

This PR does NOT implement `experts` + `shared_expert` joint online quantization + fusion. `experts` is expected to be already quantized in this PR (loaded through `QuarkOCP_MX_MoEMethod`/`INCMxfp4MoEMethod`)

Main design goal is to be as much as possible quant method agnostic.

We also preserve quant config compatibility checks for fused shared expert, that could be extended to accommodate new precisions e.g. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53161

## Test Plan

Testing:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES="6,7" \
vllm serve \
    amd/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4 \
    --quantization-config.targets '{"*shared_expert*": "mxfp4"}' \
    --tensor-parallel-size 2
```

`pytest tests/quantization/test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py -s -vvvvv`

`test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py` passing `7 passed, 14 warnings in 10.31s`
